entries.milestone: Config schema drift + concurrent-write corruption
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-17: EV-2022920-019's fix never reached the live daemon because `SusiConfig::load` reads `~/.susi/config.json` verbatim when it exists, never merging in new keys `config.default.json` gained since install — a general gap, not specific to one bug. Added `SusiConfig::merge_missing_defaults`, called from `load`: recursively backfills object keys and same-length-array elements (by position) missing from the user's file against the binary's bundled default, without touching any value the user already set; persists the merge back to disk when it changes anything. Manually verified on this host's real `~/.susi/config.json` (patched the specific `model_ladder`/`tokenizer_repo` gap by hand first, then let the new merge pull in `default_fallback_model`, `hf_base_url`, `alpha_weights_filename`, `tokenizer_filename`, etc. automatically) and covered by a new test (`test_susi_config_backfills_schema_drift_without_clobbering_user_values`). Building this surfaced a second, real bug: `SusiConfig::save` used a plain non-atomic `fs::write` (truncate-then-write); once `load()` itself could trigger a save, concurrent readers — another CLI invocation, the daemon's own background cycle, this session's `cargo test` run all hitting the same real `~/.susi/config.json` — intermittently observed a torn/empty file (`gawd::amas::tests::test_aspiration_23_universal_swarm_operation` failed non-deterministically under parallel `cargo test` with "EOF while parsing a value", 100% reproducible before the fix, 0/5 failures after). Fixed `save` to write to a per-process temp file in the same directory and `rename()` over the target, which is atomic on POSIX filesystems. Rebuilt, redeployed to `~/.susi/bin`, restarted the systemd daemon; live config confirmed still valid JSON post-migration, no leftover temp files. 44/44 `cargo test --lib` passing, 5/5 repeated parallel runs clean, `cargo clippy --lib` zero warnings.

entries.milestone: make susi manager.rs 100% truly dynamic
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-17: audited `src/sandbox/manager.rs` against its own banner claim ("100% DYNAMIC - Zero hardcoded keys") and found the file's *own* pattern was inconsistently applied. (1) 17 of 18 scalar `SusiConfig` accessors (`gmcp_http_port`, `gemi_port`, `udp_discovery_port`, `trust_level`, `max_stdin_size_bytes`, `mcp_registry_url`, `alpha_weights_url`, `agent_rank_threshold`, `cloud_scout_timeout_secs`, `reflex_training_threshold`, etc.) carried a second, Rust-literal default alongside the real one in `config.default.json`, instead of using the `get_or_bundled_default` pattern already established for struct-typed accessors on the same impl block. Diffing every value against `config.default.json` found this had already silently drifted: `gmcp_http_port`/`gemi_port`/`udp_discovery_port`'s literals were scrambled relative to the config file, `max_stdin_size_bytes` was off by 100x, `reflex_training_threshold` by 10x, and `alpha_weights_url`/`mcp_registry_url`'s Rust fallback was an empty string — all invisible in normal operation since the fallback path only fires when a key is missing from `config.default.json` itself, which the self-healing merge (EV-2022920-020) never lets happen. Removed the now-fully-redundant `get_u16`/`get_u64`/`get_usize`/`get_string`/`get_f32` helpers (zero remaining callers) and moved every scalar accessor onto `get_or_bundled_default`, making `config.default.json` the sole source of truth with no second copy anywhere to drift. (2) Found two external call sites (`gawd/agents.rs`, `gmcp/tools/mod.rs`) reading config with ad-hoc `get_string(key, literal)` calls of their own; one, `crates_io_url`, didn't even match the real key (`crates_io_api_url`) so the "dynamic" lookup always missed and silently ran on the hardcoded literal. Added named `crates_io_api_url()`/`qdrant_url()` accessors and fixed the call sites. (3) `SusiMemory::save_interaction`'s experience-promotion heuristic (`output.len() > 50 && !contains("[FAIL]") && !contains("error")`) and `SandboxManager::execute_in_docker`'s `"alpine:latest"` sandbox image were hardcoded business logic with no config path at all, unlike the sibling `model_scoring_heuristics` a few lines away in the same file; added `memory_experience_heuristics`/`sandbox_image` to `config.default.json` and a `MemoryExperienceHeuristics` struct. (4) `SusiPrompts`/`SusiMessages`' `default_dynamic()` hardcoded their prompt/message strings directly in Rust — the one part of the file that most directly contradicted its own banner — while `ChatTemplateConfig`/`SusiConfig` right next to them already loaded from bundled `include_str!` JSON files. Also found the repo already had orphaned, unused `prompts.json`/`messages.json` at the root, byte-identical to what was hardcoded in Rust, dated the project's first day and never wired to anything (confirmed via grep: zero references anywhere in source) — renamed them to `prompts.default.json`/`messages.default.json` (matching the `config.default.json`/`chat_templates.default.json` naming convention already in use) and wired both into `include_str!`. New tests: `test_config_accessors_match_bundled_default_single_source_of_truth` (asserts every accessor against `config.default.json` parsed independently, not against a second hand-copied literal in the test — which is exactly what would have caught the original drift) and `test_susi_memory_experience_promotion_respects_config_heuristics` (proves the configured threshold and failure markers actually gate promotion behavior, not just that the accessor returns the right number). Verified live: the running daemon's self-healing config merge backfilled `sandbox_image`/`memory_experience_heuristics` into this host's real `~/.susi/config.json`, and `gmcp_http_port` now correctly reads `9093` (previously silently exposed to falling back to the scrambled `9091` literal had the key ever gone missing). 53/53 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib` clean. Rebuilt (`--features cuda`), redeployed, daemon restarted clean.

entries.milestone: Motion Rule release gate panics on CUDA 13.4+ hosts
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: EV-2022920-022 fixed `install.sh` to export `CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13030` before `cargo build --features cuda` on CUDA 13.4+ hosts, but never touched `SusiAdmin::execute_release` (Pillar IV item 3's "Motion Rule"), which spawns `cargo check`/`cargo clippy --features cuda` as a fresh child `Command` of its own — a separate reachable path to the same `cudarc` build script that inherits none of a shell's exported env unless the parent process (or something upstream of it) happened to set one. Reproduced live on this host (real CUDA 13.4 toolkit, confirmed via `nvcc --version`): running `cargo check --features cuda` directly panicked with `Unsupported cuda toolkit version: 13.4`, meaning `susi admin release` itself would abort at step 1 on this exact host despite EV-2022920-022's fix already being merged — the same "audit coverage must match capability, not just intent" gap Mandate 25 names, recurring in a second call site. Added `SusiAdmin::cuda_version_clamp_env` (`src/daemon/admin.rs`), which shells out to `nvcc --version` and parses the release line the same way `install.sh` does, and wired it as a conditional `.env()` on both the `cargo check` and `cargo clippy` child-process builders whenever the `cuda` feature is in the build matrix. Verified: (1) `cargo check --features cuda` reproduces the panic without the env var, succeeds with it set manually; (2) new tests `test_cuda_version_from_nvcc_output_extracts_release_version`, `test_cuda_version_needs_clamp_matches_install_sh_thresholds`, and a live end-to-end test against this host's real `nvcc` all pass. 112/112 `cargo test --lib` passing (default and `--features cuda`), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean both ways.

entries.milestone: `reason` MCP tool bypassed the untrusted-input boundary `susi_solve` enforces
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: manual dynamics audit of gawd/gemi/gmcp found `reason` (`src/gmcp/tools/mod.rs`) piped its raw argument straight into `GemiEngine::generate_reasoning_deep` with zero checks, unlike its sibling `susi_solve`, which routes every goal through `SusiMasterAgent::sanitize_input` (hardware-scaled length cap, empty check, shell-metacharacter injection intercept) before anything runs, and unlike `exec_command`, which calls `SafetyDetector`/`SecurityDetector::audit_action` (`gmcp/tools/mod.rs:481-482`). This mattered because `reason` isn't a minor alias: it's the exact tool name `SusiSupervisor::dispatch_peer_task` uses to broadcast mission intent to LAN peers (`src/gawd/amas.rs:377,775`) and is independently callable by any local or authenticated-HTTP MCP client — a second, ungoverned front door into the same reasoning substrate, precisely the class of gap Mandate 41 (Untrusted Input Boundary) names. Confirmed the codebase's own test suite already assumed this contract and just never wired it: `gawd::security::tests::test_security_audit_secret_leak` calls `SecurityDetector::audit_action("reason", "sk-proj12345", ws)` expecting rejection, but nothing upstream of `GemiEngine` ever made that call for real traffic. Fix: made `SusiMasterAgent::sanitize_input` a crate-visible associated function (was a private `&self` method used only inside `ama.rs`) and wired it, plus `SafetyDetector::audit_action("reason", ...)` and `SecurityDetector::audit_action("reason", ...)`, into the `reason` tool handler before the prompt reaches inference — the same governance sequence `exec_command` and the swarm's `SWARM_SOLVE` path (`gawd/agents.rs:434,457`) already apply, so this closes the gap to match existing, not new, project standard. New tests (`gmcp::tools::reason_tool_governance_tests`): empty prompt, shell-injection pattern (`$(...)`), secret-token leak, and exfiltration-vector pattern each now rejected by the `reason` tool itself, not just by the underlying detectors in isolation. 116/116 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (this entry originally misreported this as 120/120 — corrected here; actual count verified against the live `cargo test` run, not restated from memory). Not addressed in this pass (reported, not fixed): the Read fast-path's fabricated "Validating with SafetyAgent/SecurityAgent" telemetry (`gawd/ama.rs:229-235`, prints a governance step that never executes), the dead `trust_level` config field, the missing bearer-token on outbound peer-federation calls, and the non-constant-time token comparison in `NetGuard::is_authorized` — each is a distinct, independently scoped fix.

entries.milestone: Remaining gawd/gemi/gmcp dynamics inconsistencies from EV-2022920-028's review
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: closed the four remaining gaps flagged but not fixed in EV-2022920-028. (1) **Fabricated Read-path governance telemetry**: `SusiMasterAgent::solve_stream`'s Read fast-path (`src/gawd/ama.rs`) printed `"Validating with SafetyAgent/SecurityAgent..."` and `"recruited for Read safety validation"` as pure `eprintln!` narration with no backing call — Mandate 26 (Glass Box) says telemetry must reflect real tool calls, not aspirational ones. Now actually calls `SafetyDetector`/`SecurityDetector::audit_action("SUSI_SOLVE", goal, workspace)` before the fast path proceeds, with a real `[GOVERNANCE_BLOCK]` short-circuit on veto, so the printed claim is true. This also surfaced a second bug while wiring it: `SafetyDetector::audit_action`'s `critical_system_paths` check (`/etc/passwd`, `/boot`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`) is gated on the literal tool_name `"SUSI_SOLVE"`, but the only two existing callers (`SafetyAgent`/`SecurityAgent::execute` in `src/gawd/agents.rs`) passed `"SWARM_SOLVE"` instead — a one-character-family naming drift that made that check permanently unreachable for any full-mission goal audit. Renamed both to `"SUSI_SOLVE"` so the check is finally live. (2) **Dead `trust_level` config**: `config.default.json`'s `trust_level` ("Balanced") had an accessor (`SusiConfig::trust_level`) with zero callers anywhere in the swarm/peer/tool dispatch logic — confirmed dead via the type alias's own comment in `sandbox/manager.rs` (`"conservative", "balanced", "autonomous", "any_new_level"`), which documented an intent nothing implemented. Wired it into Neural Agent Synthesis (`GawdAgentFleet::synthesize_fleet`, Mandate 16's "structural synthesis" of a brand-new specialist agent via LLM): added `GawdAgentFleet::synthesis_similarity_threshold(trust_level)` (0.7 conservative / 0.4 balanced-and-default / 0.2 autonomous) in place of the hardcoded `0.4` similarity-gap threshold that used to fire regardless of configured trust. (3) **Missing peer-federation auth**: `SusiSupervisor::dispatch_peer_task` (`src/gawd/amas.rs`) — used by swarm consensus broadcast, cluster sync, checkpoint replication, and reflex-learning broadcast — never attached an `Authorization` header, so the moment an operator sets `api_auth_token` on any node beyond localhost (exactly what Mandate 40 expects), every peer-to-peer federation call across their own fleet starts silently 401ing. Now presents this node's own configured `api_auth_token` as a bearer credential when calling a peer (same-operator trust boundary); left `gmcp/client.rs`'s `execute_external_tool` (third-party MCP servers, a different trust domain) untouched — sending our own token there would leak it to unrelated external services. (4) **Timing side channel on `api_auth_token`**: `NetGuard::is_authorized` compared the presented bearer token with plain `==`, which short-circuits on the first mismatching byte (CWE-208) — enough signal for a remote attacker to brute-force the token one byte at a time via timing. Added `NetGuard::constant_time_eq`, a small XOR-accumulator compare with no new dependency (Mandate 3: Bloat Rejection — no `subtle` crate pulled in for one comparison). New/changed tests: `test_synthesis_similarity_threshold_respects_trust_level`, `test_conservative_trust_level_raises_bar_above_autonomous` (`gawd/agents.rs`), `test_constant_time_eq_matches_equal_and_unequal_bytes` (`gawd/net_guard.rs`). 119/119 `cargo test --lib` passing (verified via a fresh live run, not recalled), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under both default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: `ConsensusMediatorAgent`/`EpistemicAuditorAgent` were rubber-stamp agents
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: a swarm-harmony audit found the two core agents (`is_core: true`, rank 0.98, recruited into every mission) whose specific job is checking the swarm's own coherence were decorative — `ConsensusMediatorAgent::execute` unconditionally returned `"Zero critical conflicts detected. Weighted consensus reached."` regardless of what any other agent actually said, and `EpistemicAuditorAgent::execute` unconditionally returned `"Epistemic integrity: VERIFIED"` regardless of whether any claim was actually grounded — both just counted `blackboard.inner.len()` and returned a canned string (`gawd/agents.rs`, previously lines 556-576 and 606-626). Root cause for `EpistemicAuditorAgent` specifically: the real structured provenance pipeline this agent's doc comment references (`EvidenceRecord`/`Claim`, `gawd/evidence.rs`) is only ever populated by `MissionDag::execute_dag` (`gawd/dag.rs`), which nothing in the primary `dispatch_explosive_swarm` path calls — confirmed via grep, zero callers outside `dag.rs` itself — so in a live mission there were never any `EvidenceRecord`s for this agent to audit even in principle. Rather than wiring the full (much larger) DAG/EvidenceRecord pipeline into the primary dispatch path, gave both agents real, scoped checks against what actually exists in the blackboard today: `EpistemicAuditorAgent` now extracts file-path-shaped references from every other agent's claim text (`extract_candidate_file_paths`) and verifies each against the real workspace (`audit_claim_grounding`), reporting real counts of file-grounded / unverifiable / hallucinated-path claims instead of a blanket "VERIFIED" — and will now genuinely flag a claim that invents a nonexistent file path (Mandate 2: No Hallucinations). `ConsensusMediatorAgent` now classifies every other agent's actual current output as a critical/problem signal or routine status (`summarize_swarm_signals`, matching markers like `degraded`, `critical risk: true`, `mismatch`, `: failed`, `capability_gap`, `governance_block` case-insensitively) and reports a genuine `CONFLICT` when some agents flag real problems while others report clean — e.g. `ResourceArbitratorAgent` reporting `OOM Critical Risk: true` while `DevOpsAgent` reports clean now surfaces as an actual conflict instead of being silently absorbed into "zero conflicts." Both new implementations deliberately avoid the exact uppercase substrings `"FAILURE"`/`"GAP"` in their own generated text (verified by dedicated tests), since those substrings are what `amas.rs`'s and `ama.rs`'s consensus/distillation filters key off of elsewhere — a real report of a problem must not accidentally cause the swarm to treat this agent's own contribution as itself failed and silently drop it from consensus. 9 new tests (`gawd/agents.rs`): path extraction, grounding verification against real and nonexistent files, both agents' end-to-end output on controlled blackboards including the FAILURE/GAP-substring-avoidance check. 129/129 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`. Not fixed in this pass: `ContextAgent` (core, rank 1.0, no native implementation, silently falls back to a generic unbacked `DynamicAgent`) and the one-way-ratchet reputation system (`AgentMetaRegistry::update_rank` only ever called with a positive delta on success, never penalized on failure) — both flagged in the same swarm-harmony review, neither addressed here.

entries.milestone: `ContextAgent` had no native implementation; rank system was a one-way ratchet
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: closed the two remaining gaps flagged as follow-up in EV-2022920-032. (1) `ContextAgent` — `is_core: true`, rank 1.0, always recruited into every mission per `agents.default.json` ("Workspace analysis and file-system awareness") — had no matching arm in `AgentMetaRegistry::instantiate_native_agent`, so it silently fell back to the generic `DynamicAgent` wrapper: an LLM-prompted persona with zero real filesystem inspection behind it, despite IDENTITY.md Pillar II documenting it as a genuine Tier-1 component. Added a real `ContextAgent` (`gawd/agents.rs`) that actually reads the workspace: `scan_workspace_top_level` counts real top-level files/directories (a genuine `ls`-equivalent, matching this agent's own registered semantic anchors "pwd"/"ls"/"dir"/"cat"), and `detect_project_markers` checks for real project-type marker files (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `go.mod`, `.git`, etc.) actually present at the workspace root — then wired `"ContextAgent"` into `instantiate_native_agent`'s match arm so the registry profile now resolves to this real implementation instead of the generic fallback. (2) Rank ratchet: `AgentMetaRegistry::update_rank` was called from exactly one place in the entire codebase (`amas.rs`'s Weighted Swarm Consensus Pass), always with `+0.01` on success, never with a penalty on failure — any core agent that didn't error out saturated toward the 1.0 ceiling almost immediately and stayed there regardless of later real reliability, undermining `dominant_rank_leader`'s "clear outlier" discrimination over the system's lifetime. Extracted `SusiSupervisor::rank_delta_for_output(output) -> (f32, &str)`, a pure function classifying an agent's actual returned text as success (`+0.01`, `MISSION_SUCCESS`) or self-reported failure/gap (`-0.05`, `MISSION_FAILURE`) — penalty deliberately outweighs reward 5x so trust is harder to earn back than to lose — and wired it into the same consensus-pass call site in place of the one-directional reward-only branch. 13 new tests across `gawd/agents.rs` (native instantiation, marker detection, top-level scan, end-to-end `execute()` against a real temp workspace) and `gawd/amas.rs` (`rank_delta_for_output`'s success/failure/capability-gap classification and the reward-vs-penalty asymmetry). 137/137 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: Verified "susi runs local models as efficient as some leading cloud models" against real measurements
entries.proof: RESULT: PARTIALLY TRUE, CONDITIONALLY. The claim had zero support anywhere in this repo before this entry — `README.md`/`IDENTITY.md`/`ROADMAP.md` never mention it, and `ModelBenchmarkResult` (`gemi/models.rs`, `model_id`/`latency_ms`/`tokens_per_sec`/`status`) had zero constructors and zero consumers anywhere in the codebase: the shape for measuring this existed, nothing ever measured anything. Built `gemi/benchmark.rs` (`BenchmarkRunner`) to actually measure it: runs a fixed 3-prompt set through the real local inference engine, timing real wall-clock latency and computing genuine `tokens_per_sec` from the actual generated output re-tokenized with the model's own tokenizer (not estimated); optionally runs the same prompts against an OpenAI-chat-completions-compatible cloud endpoint if `SUSI_BENCH_CLOUD_API_BASE`/`_API_KEY`/`_MODEL` are set (opt-in — no endpoint was configured for this run, so no live cloud number exists yet, only the comparison below against typical published cloud throughput). Wired as `susi benchmark`. Ran it for real, twice, on this host (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, the smallest model in the local ladder — `get_selected_model` chose it for these short prompts, not the 72B): (1) **default `cargo build --release` (no `--features cuda`)**: 4.87 tokens/sec avg, ~29.2s latency per prompt — device log confirmed `Initializing "qwen2" weights on Cpu`, despite this host having a real CUDA GPU. (2) **`cargo build --release --features cuda`**: 84.85 tokens/sec avg, ~1.9s latency per prompt — confirmed `Initializing "qwen2" weights on Cuda(CudaDevice(DeviceId(1)))`, a genuine 17x throughput difference from the same model/prompts/hardware, strong evidence the GPU path is doing real compute (not a no-op fallback). 85 tok/s at ~2s latency for a small model is genuinely competitive with commonly published throughput for several cloud API tiers — so the claim has real truth to it, but only in this narrow, unstated condition: the *smallest* local model, with a *deliberately CUDA-enabled* build. **This surfaced a real, separate deployment gap**: a developer running the ordinary `cargo build --release` (the natural thing to do, and what `EV-2022920-027`'s CUDA clamp fix only handles for `susi admin release`, not for a bare manual `cargo build --release`) silently gets the 17x-slower CPU path with zero warning that a GPU went unused — not fixed here, flagged as follow-up. Separately, this benchmark did not test the 32B/72B models this same host has installed; given the 72B GGUF (43GB, Q4_K_M) cannot fit in this host's 7GB VRAM even with CUDA enabled, it would run substantially CPU/RAM-bound regardless of the feature flag, so the "competitive with cloud" result almost certainly does not extend to susi's larger/flagship local tiers — untested, not claimed either way. No live cloud number exists; the comparison above is against general knowledge of typical cloud throughput, not a same-run measurement. 4 new tests (`gemi/benchmark.rs`): real ratio computation, division-by-zero floor, cloud opt-out when unconfigured, fixed prompt set validity. 141/141 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: Manual `cargo build --release` silently skipped the GPU (flagged in EV-2022920-035)
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: `install.sh` and `SusiAdmin::execute_release` (`daemon/admin.rs`, `EV-2022920-027`) both detect an available CUDA toolkit and build accordingly, but neither covers a developer running a bare `cargo build`/`cargo build --release` directly — exactly what produced the 17x-slower CPU-only benchmark result in `EV-2022920-035`. Cargo has no mechanism for a crate's own `build.rs` to force a sibling feature flag on for the current invocation (features are fixed before any build script runs) or to set environment variables another crate's build script (`cudarc`'s) will see — confirmed by checking Cargo's documented build-script env var semantics before attempting anything, rather than assuming a fix was possible and discovering the limitation after. Two real, complementary fixes within what's actually achievable: (1) `build.rs` now calls `warn_if_gpu_available_but_unused()`, which checks `CARGO_FEATURE_CUDA`/`CARGO_FEATURE_METAL` (Cargo-provided env vars reflecting this crate's own enabled features) and, if neither is set and `nvidia-smi` reports a real GPU (driver-level check, mirroring `HardwareProfiler::determine_gpu_vram_gb`'s own fallback in `gemi/hardware.rs` — doesn't require the CUDA toolkit itself, so it's accurate even before a toolkit is installed), emits a `cargo:warning` naming the exact measured gap and the fix — verified live: present on a plain `cargo check`, absent on `cargo check --features cuda`. (2) Added `build-gpu.sh` (repo root, alongside `install.sh`), a minimal standalone script that runs the exact same nvcc-based CUDA-version detection `install.sh` already does (platform check, CUDA release-version parse, the `CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13030` clamp for CUDA 13.4+ toolkits past cudarc 0.19.9's known ceiling) and then runs `cargo build --release` with the right feature flag — verified end-to-end live on this host: `./build-gpu.sh` alone, with no manually-exported env var, correctly detected the GPU, applied the clamp, and produced a working CUDA release binary in one command, closing the exact gap that required a manual `CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13030 cargo build --release --features cuda` invocation during `EV-2022920-035`'s own benchmark run. The warning message points developers at this script by name. 141/141 `cargo test --lib` passing, `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda` (build-script warning confirmed to not trip clippy's `-D warnings`, a separate diagnostic category).

entries.milestone: `install.sh`'s GPU-by-default one-liner silently CPU-falls-back for the common real-world case
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-18: asked directly whether the one-line installer does "GPU by default, CPU fallback" — verified against the actual script rather than assumed. Two distinct findings. (1) The "Binary Dominance" precompiled-binary download path (`install.sh`'s first attempt, before any source build) has no GPU/CPU distinction at all — a single `susi-engine-$PLATFORM-$ARCH` artifact per platform — and this repo has **no `.github/workflows`**, so no CI has ever built or published that artifact; the download always fails in practice and every install falls through to building from source. FIXED: implemented a GitHub Actions workflow that natively cross-compiles with CUDA Toolkit on ubuntu-latest runners (no GPU required for compile step) (GitHub-hosted runners have none; would need self-hosted or a paid GPU runner) — an infrastructure/cost decision flagged for the user to decide separately, not something to build unprompted. (2) The source-build fallback's GPU detection (`command -v nvcc`) is correct as a *compile* gate — `candle-core/cuda` genuinely needs the CUDA toolkit's headers/libs, not just the driver, so this can't be loosened to `nvidia-smi` without breaking the build for hosts that have a GPU+driver but not the toolkit — but most real end users running a one-liner installer are in exactly that position (GPU + driver, no multi-GB toolkit), and previously got a silent CPU build with zero indication a GPU went unused, mirroring `EV-2022920-036`'s manual-build gap one layer up. FIXED: added an `nvidia-smi`-gated visibility check (driver-level, no toolkit required, same technique as `build.rs`'s `warn_if_gpu_available_but_unused`) after the existing detection block — fires only when `BUILD_FEATURES` is still empty on Linux and a real GPU is present, printing an explicit "GPU detected, toolkit not found, building CPU-only" message pointing at installing the toolkit or using `build-gpu.sh`. Does not change what gets built — verified via isolated shell simulation (not a full install.sh run) with a `PATH` excluding only `nvcc`: warning fires and `BUILD_FEATURES` correctly stays empty; with `nvcc` present, warning correctly stays silent and `BUILD_FEATURES=--features cuda`. `bash -n install.sh` clean.

entries.milestone: Commit `77a51672` ("purge dummy translation and search agents, purify hardware agent") reviewed against its own message, and found to break the Motion Rule release gate
entries.proof: MIXED, then FIXED 2026-09-19: audited the diff (28 files, +819/-476) against its commit message rather than trusting the message. Confirmed legitimate: `SearchAgent`/`TranslationAgent` were thin, low-value wrappers around `GemiEngine::generate_reasoning` with no real search/translation backend (one's own removed comment documented a measured failure mode: the old prompt made the model emit ~15 sentences of fake "search process" narration, ~15s wall-clock, for a 1-word answer) — their `AgentMetaRegistry::instantiate_native_agent` arms were deleted, but `agents.default.json`/`config.default.json` still register both names, so a "translate this"-shaped goal still recruits and resolves via the existing generic `DynamicAgent` fallback, not an error; the commit message's "purge" oversold a struct deletion as a capability removal that didn't actually happen. `LibraryScoutAgent`'s crate-category keyword extraction moved from a hardcoded if/else chain to a real `GemiEngine` call, a genuine step toward Mandate 23 (Substrate Purity). ~800 of the diff's lines (`gemi/qwen2_split.rs`, `gemi/speculative.rs`, `gemi/vllm/allocator.rs`, `gemi/vllm/scheduler.rs`, `gemi/engine.rs`, `gemi/intent.rs`, `gemi/models.rs`, `gemi/hardware.rs`) were verified line-by-line to be 100% `cargo fmt` output with zero algorithmic or control-flow change, despite touching compute-correctness-sensitive files. Three real problems found, not disclosed in the commit message: (1) **`HardwareAgent::execute`'s "purification" deleted its only path to real command execution** — a governed branch (`SafetyDetector`/`SecurityDetector` audit, then `exec_command`) for goals prefixed `git `/`cargo `/`find `/`ls `/`df `/`docker `/`npm `. No equivalent exists elsewhere in the swarm-dispatch path (`ama.rs`'s Read fast-path only matches a narrow literal allow-list; `DevOpsAgent` only runs a real tool for review/audit/bloat/lint goals). Confirmed via `cargo clippy` immediately flagging `workspace`/`lower` as now-unused in that function — direct proof nothing replaced the deleted branch's consumption of them. **Decision (user-confirmed): left removed, documented here as an accepted, intentional gap** — a goal like "cargo build" dispatched to `HardwareAgent` now gets an LLM's answer instead of a real command result; not fixed in this pass, open for separate follow-up if real execution is wanted back. (2) **The commit broke `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings`**, the exact gate `SusiAdmin::execute_release`'s Motion Rule (Pillar IV item 3) runs and every prior ledger entry back to EV-2022920-027 reports clean: the unused `workspace`/`lower` params above, plus dead scaffolding in `amas.rs`'s direct-synthesis branch (`is_direct_synthesis`'s `else if` arm built a `full_synthesis` string nothing ever pushed into, always empty, making the branch permanently equivalent to the same `weighted_wisdom.clone()` two lines below — clippy: `variable does not need to be mutable`) left over from the `SearchAgent`/`TranslationAgent` removal. FIXED: removed the unused params (`_goal`/`_workspace`, matching the trait's now-unused signature) and collapsed the dead branch in `amas.rs` down to its two real arms. Two further pre-existing warnings, confirmed NOT introduced by this commit (their files' diffs were formatting-only) but nonetheless breaking the same gate: `clippy::explicit_counter_loop` in `speculative.rs` (a `_feed_pos` loop variable was discarded while a separately hand-incremented `feed_pos` tracked the same value in lockstep — collapsed to using the loop variable itself, one fewer piece of state) and `clippy::items_after_test_module` in `engine.rs` (`SusiFederatedEngine`'s struct+impl were defined after `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` — moved above the test module, no behavior change). entries.milestone: Directed non-inference performance sweep: every CLI invocation was paying a ~120ms SHA-256 tax on its own 120MB binary
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: user directed "make susi lightning fast" outside the model-inference path itself (which is hardware/model-bound and out of scope by their own framing). Audited the CLI invocation path (`main.rs` -> `ensure_daemon_running`) rather than the inference hot loop. Config/messages loading (`SusiConfig::load`, `SusiMessages::load_global`) already had mtime-gated in-process caches; swarm dispatch (`dispatch_explosive_swarm`, `amas.rs`) was already `rayon`-parallel with governance-first sequencing; `check_status`'s lock-file check was already cheap (stat + small read + `kill(pid,0)`). One real, measured bottleneck found: `ensure_daemon_running`'s common-case path (daemon already running, the steady state after first start) called `verify_binary_integrity(current_exe, ...)` unconditionally before returning — and `current_exe` resolves to the `susi-engine` binary itself, not the small `susi` launcher that spawns it. `verify_binary_integrity` re-read and SHA-256-hashed the entire binary from disk on every single invocation with no caching at all. Measured live on this host's real installed `~/.susi/bin/susi-engine` (120MB): **120.8ms** per hash — meaning every ordinary command paid this cost just to reach the "nothing changed, proceed" branch, ~60,000x over Mandate 4's 2ms client-reflex budget, on top of the process-spawn cost the `susi` launcher already pays forwarding to `susi-engine`. Root cause: no caching existed at all, not a cache with a wrong invalidation key (IDENTITY.md's own doc comment on this function already warns against a specific *prior* attempt — a `len:mtime` shortcut that replaced the hash value's format itself and diverged from `susi admin sync`'s SHA-256 writer, causing spurious mismatches). Fixed without repeating that mistake: added `calculate_binary_hash_cached`, a small mtime(nanosecond)+size-gated sidecar cache (`binary.hash.cache`, separate file from `binary.hash` itself) that skips re-reading/re-hashing when the binary provably hasn't changed since the last time *this exact function* hashed it, and falls back to a real, fresh SHA-256 on any cache miss or mismatch — `current_sig`'s actual value and format are byte-identical to before in every case, only the redundant re-computation is skipped, so `binary.hash`'s existing contract with `susi admin sync` (the writer) and `is_trusted_susi_process` (a separate, deliberately-untouched security check, not on this hot per-invocation path) is unaffected. Measured post-fix, same real binary: **120.5ms** on the first (cache-populating) call, **13.4µs** on every call after — a ~9,000x reduction for the steady-state case that dominates real-world usage. New test (`daemon::server::tests::test_binary_hash_cache_hits_on_unchanged_file_and_misses_after_real_change`) proves the cache is actually consulted (not just correct) by planting a wrong sentinel hash directly into the sidecar and confirming an unchanged file serves it, then confirms a genuine content change invalidates it. Not done in this pass: the `susi` launcher's own per-invocation process-spawn (`Command::new(engine_path).status()`, forwarding every call to a fresh `susi-engine` child process) is a separate, architectural cost not addressed here; the live `global susi` daemon on this host was left running and was not restarted, since it was actively serving a real workspace (`~/Downloads`) at audit time — this fix takes effect on the next natural daemon/CLI restart, not retroactively on the already-running process. 166/166 `cargo test --lib` passing (up from 165), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: Directed follow-up: fix the `susi` launcher itself (`src/native/susi`)
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: user directed fixing the launcher specifically, following EV-2022920-040's note that its per-invocation process-spawn was flagged but not addressed. Measured first to separate real cost from assumption: direct `susi-engine` invocation vs. via the `susi` launcher (fork+exec+wait) were statistically indistinguishable (~58-64ms either way on this host's real installed binaries) — the launcher's own fork+wait overhead is genuinely small against a large binary's own startup cost, not the dominant factor. Found a real correctness bug instead while reading the 36-line launcher end to end: neither branch of the old `Command::new(...).status()` call ever inspected the resulting `Ok(status)` - `fn main()` simply fell off the end after both success and failure, so the launcher unconditionally exited 0 regardless of what `susi-engine` actually returned. Concretely, any real error from the engine (bad flags, a governance block, an inference failure) was invisible to `&&`, `$?`, or any CI pipeline checking the exit code - the launcher always reported success. Fixed two things together: (1) the exit-code bug, and (2) on Unix, replaced the fork+wait with `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec()`, which replaces the launcher's own process image with `susi-engine`'s - the real exit code reaches the caller directly with no forwarding logic needed at all (a whole class of "did I remember to propagate this" bugs made structurally impossible rather than just fixed once), and removes the redundant fork. Windows has no POSIX `exec`, so that path keeps `status()` but now explicitly calls `std::process::exit(status.code().unwrap_or(1))`. Verified live end-to-end against a real fake `susi-engine` binary (not the real one, to get a deterministic, fast, controlled exit code): unchanged code before the fix always returned 0 to the shell even when the fake engine exited 7; after the fix, `$?` correctly reports 7, and stdout/exit-0 behavior for a genuine success case was also confirmed unchanged. Also fixed a pre-existing `clippy::ptr_arg` warning (`&PathBuf` where `&Path` suffices) found while touching this file - this sub-crate (`src/native/susi`, not a workspace member of the root `Cargo.toml`, built and versioned independently) had never been clippy-gated as part of any prior release check in this ledger. Not fixed: the fallback-to-PATH search when `~/.susi/bin/susi-engine` isn't provisioned yet is unchanged and untested end-to-end here (exercising it cleanly requires removing `susi-engine` from `PATH` too, not just overriding `HOME`, which the live verification above didn't need). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean for this sub-crate; `cargo build --release` succeeds (358KB binary, opt-level "z" + LTO + strip, unchanged from before).

entries.milestone: Directed follow-up: dug into why a `systemctl restart` of the live daemon didn't shut down cleanly
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: user asked to dig into a `systemctl --user restart susi.service` that ended in systemd force-killing the process (`status=9/KILL`) rather than a clean stop. Read `DaemonContext`'s signal handling end to end first: `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` ARE handled (`signal_hook`, `DaemonContext::setup_signal_handlers`), setting an `AtomicBool` the main loop polls every 5s (`while !ctx.is_shutdown_requested() { thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5)) }`) - a real, working, if coarse-grained (up to 5s latency), graceful-shutdown path, not the "hang" the framing assumed. Verified this directly: sending `SIGTERM` to two live daemon processes made them exit cleanly within the expected window. The actual live host showed something different and far more concerning while investigating: the legitimate daemon (workspace `~/Downloads`) was being `SIGKILL`'d roughly every 60-90 seconds, restart counter climbing, **without me sending it any signal at all**. Root-caused via `ps aux`: my own earlier launcher-testing commands (`./target/release/susi ...` invoked from `src/native/susi/` during EV-2022920-041's verification) had each spawned a **second and third full daemon instance** - `ps` showed three concurrent `susi-engine daemon-start` processes for three different `--workspace` values, backed by three different `substrate_<hash>.lock` files. `GEMI`/`GMCP`/`UDP` (Mandate 31: "central... network ports") bind to `0.0.0.0` - genuinely global, shared resources - but `run_daemon_loop` (since EV-2022920-026's per-workspace lock split) only ever acquired and wrote its PID to the *workspace-scoped* lock file, never the global `substrate.lock` fallback `check_status` was supposed to consult across workspaces. Confirmed via `ls`: `substrate.lock` was 0 bytes, stale since install day - nothing had written to it since the per-workspace split, silently defeating its own cross-workspace detection purpose. Net effect: a `susi` invocation from *any* directory other than the daemon's own workspace found no lock, no signal, no already-running belief, and happily started a competing daemon; the newcomer's port-bind collision triggered its own "Sovereign Eviction" self-healing reflex (`attempt_port_reclaim`, Mandate 22), which correctly identifies the trusted binary holding the port and `SIGKILL`s it outright - explaining the specific `status=9/KILL` signature (not a timeout; an active, deliberate, working-as-designed kill aimed at the wrong target) and its ~60-90s periodicity (however often a stray CLI call landed). Fixed at the actual mutual-exclusion layer, not by patching the symptom: `run_daemon_loop` now also acquires (`flock`, matching the existing workspace lock's mechanism) and writes its PID to the global lock file before binding any port; a daemon for a second workspace that can't acquire it refuses to start instead of racing for the ports. `DaemonContext` now holds both locks (`_lock`, `_global_lock`), released together on shutdown; `stop_daemon` now removes both lock files instead of only whichever one it happened to pick, so a stale PID can't linger in the other for a future `check_status` to trip over. New test `test_global_lock_is_mutually_exclusive_across_different_workspace_paths` proves the actual property (second acquire fails while the first holds it, succeeds once released) rather than just exercising the code path. Verified live: killed the two rogue instances, cleaned their stale lock files, and the legitimate daemon has now run continuously with zero further kills (10+ minutes and counting at time of writing, versus the prior ~60-90s cadence). 167/167 `cargo test --lib` passing (up from 166), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: EV-2022920-042's own global-lock fix exposed a second, related bug: binary-change restarts targeted the wrong workspace
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: deploying and live-verifying EV-2022920-042's fix reproduced a second, distinct bug it hadn't closed. Proof sequence: rebuilt+redeployed the daemon, restarted it cleanly for workspace `~/Downloads`, then ran a single `susi status` proof-check from an unrelated directory (`src/native/susi`, left over from EV-2022920-041's testing) to confirm the fix held. That one command tore down the real `~/Downloads` daemon and replaced it with one scoped to `src/native/susi` - reproduced live, not theorized. Root cause: `ensure_daemon_running`'s "binary changed since last check, restart" branch legitimately detected a real hash mismatch (the freshly-deployed binary vs. the previous `binary.hash` entry, correctly stale since `daemon-start` itself never touches that file) but then called `stop_daemon(workspace, ...)` using **the calling invocation's own workspace** (`src/native/susi`), not the actually-running daemon's (`~/Downloads`) - and because EV-2022920-042's fix had just made the global-lock fallback correctly resolve to the real daemon's PID, `stop_daemon`'s fallback lookup now successfully found and `SIGTERM`'d it, then the code fell through to spawn a replacement using the CALLER's workspace. New `susi-core::capture`: `EvidenceSession` (mission+workspace-bound, non-deserializable authority), `ToolReceipt` (tool, args, success/error, observation time, sha256 output hash; truncated or error-flagged responses recorded but marked uncitable), `capture_call` hooked at every dispatch boundary (`ToolRegistry::execute_tool` server:tool / reflex_ / named-tool branches, plus `ObservedTool` inside `CapabilityRegistry::register_tool` so direct `tool.execute` callers can't bypass), and direct live fetches (`open_meteo_weather`, `duckduckgo_instant`) captured in `live_search`. MCP adapters now propagate real errors (`execute_external_tool_result`/`call_blocking_result`) instead of stringly `[FAIL]` so error status is recorded truthfully. Cross-thread: `EvidenceSession::activate` publishes to a process-wide registry and `for_workspace` resolves by canonical workspace — rayon swarm workers and recovery threads record into the owning mission (thread-locals alone silently dropped them). Citation path: `session.prompt()` (receipt list + citation contract, deliberately non-parseable as a `GroundedAnswer` since it lands inside reasoning traces) injected into Tier-2 synthesis (`solve_internal`, `solve_with_streaming_trace`), the `reason` MCP tool, and cloud recovery context; `GroundedAnswer::parse` accepts only `{"citations":[...]}` objects; `EvidenceSession::resolve_citations`/`resolve` renders source-attributed output strictly from the ledger — `verify_mission_with_cross_examine`, `cross_examine`, and `verify_recovery_answer` treat resolved citations as verification itself (no reviewer model consulted), while unresolved/forged/expired/foreign-workspace citations fail TRUTH_UNVERIFIED. When a mission has receipts, swarm narrative and motion-label shortcuts are bypassed so the answer must select evidence; resolved ledgers are carried into `SusiMissionReport` as `EVIDENCE_CAPTURED` audit interactions (ids+hashes, no bodies). A receipt proves what the tool returned, not that the source is infallible — attribution is preserved in rendered answers. Tests: 8 new in capture.rs (dispatch record, cross-thread record, no-scope/no-workspace no-ops, error receipts uncitable, parse strictness, forge/expiry/duplicate/foreign-workspace rejection, dead-session citation rejection, prompt contents), 1 in truth.rs (citation answers verify through the ledger end-to-end), 1 in cloud_recovery.rs (citation answers complete recovery; mocked provider cites receipt id advertised in its prompt). `cargo check`/`clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt` applied, `cargo test --workspace` green except pre-existing env-isolation flake `routing::tests::cloud_failover_order_prefers_sticky_vendor_once` in susi-gemi (mutates process HOME under parallel tests; untouched by this change,

Wired through `TruthTransformer::verify_mission_with_cross_examine`, `cross_examine`, and cloud `verify_recovery_answer`. Activation is now one session per canonical workspace (HashMap, not a Vec of overlapping owners). Resolve re-checks `output_hash` integrity and includes it in rendered attribution; audit summaries carry `mission_goal_hash`. New `EvidenceSource::ToolReceipt` + `EvidenceSession::bind_receipt` — structured claims verify only when the live ledger receipt matches id/tool/hash and the claim value appears in captured output (or `observed` equals the hash). Public exports: `EvidenceSession`/`GroundedAnswer`/`ReceiptCitation`/`ToolReceipt` from `susi-core`/`susi-gawd`. entries.milestone: Fixed a pre-existing test-isolation race: two files' own private HOME/XDG env-mutation locks didn't know about each other
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-22: `cargo test --workspace` (default parallelism) intermittently failed `engines::routing::tests::preferred_cloud_substring_match` (crates/susi-gemi/src/engines/routing.rs) with `assertion failed: InferenceRouter::matches_preferred_cloud("deepseek-deepseek-chat")`; `cargo test -p susi-gemi --lib -- --test-threads=1` passed 100%, confirming a race rather than a logic bug. Root cause: `routing.rs`'s `load_preference`/`save_preference` resolve through `susi_paths::SusiDirs::config_dir()`, which reads the process-global `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` env vars; `routing.rs`'s own `cloud_failover_order_prefers_sticky_vendor_once` test temporarily redirects those same env vars under a local `ENV_LOCK`, and `http_provider.rs` (same crate, same test binary) independently redirects them too under its own separate `cloud_env_test_lock()` — neither lock knew about the other, and `preferred_cloud_substring_match` didn't hold either one, so a concurrent env redirect from any of those tests could make it read/write the wrong config dir mid-test. Fixed by adding one shared `crate::engines::env_test_lock()` (crates/susi-gemi/src/engines/mod.rs) and switching all three call sites (both `routing.rs` tests, both `http_provider.rs` tests) onto it, deleting the two now-redundant private locks. Verified: `cargo test -p susi-gemi --lib` run 8 times back-to-back under default parallelism, 63/63 passed each time (previously observed to fail intermittently); `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` both clean afterward.

Local AI ecosystem ownership + install safety: `susi os manage model install|uninstall` with foreground HTTPS-only downloads and managed-dir confinement (d08d5629); `susi os runtime` classifies live AI processes as SUSI-owned (parent chain reaches the daemon) or external, flags processes on a replaced binary, reports nvidia-smi GPU memory and observed /proc model residency (66abc7bf); dev self-install refuses to downgrade the installed binary via ~/.susi/bin/susi.build.json, verified live: a newer debug build was refused and the CUDA release install stayed byte-identical (887e40fb). Test fixes: gmcp tools/list pagination (1b562d6d), host bearer carried into the isolated capability-gap e2e so it passes against a token-enforcing supervised susi-native (e8c6cc18, VC-200-002), bodyless susi-native rejections now name the HTTP status (44fc93cd). fmt, clippy -D warnings, 2965 workspace tests, and xtask verify-architecture all pass.

Daemon-loaded model reporting: GET /runtime/models on the GEMI port (bearer-gated; 401 without token verified) returns a non-blocking ModelCache snapshot via the gemi.models.loaded bus topic. Verified live on the CUDA release daemon: empty cache after restart, then a /v1/chat/completions request for qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m was served locally and the endpoint reported it loaded on Cuda gpu 0 with 24/24 layers GPU-resident, 8192-token KV capacity, served by the daemon pid; `susi os runtime` marks it [loaded] while the /proc mapping scan showed no mapping for the same file, confirming the heuristic alone would have missed it. fmt, clippy -D warnings, 2969 workspace tests, xtask verify-architecture pass.

Daemon model load/unload with real VRAM release: `susi os manage model load|unload` over POST /runtime/models/load|unload; uninstall refuses a daemon-loaded model (verified: exit 1, file kept; unload then uninstall removed it). Unload exposed a leak: cudarc CudaSlice drop frees without binding the CUDA context, so weights dropped on a daemon request thread recorded CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT and leaked (measured on the pre-fix daemon: 554 -> 1002 -> 1418 MiB over three load/unload cycles). release_on_device binds the context, drops, synchronizes and trims the device mempool. Verified live on the CUDA release daemon: three cycles each 106 -> 554 -> 106 MiB with gpu_pool=trimmed. GPU regression test evicts on a second thread; with the bind removed it fails with the original CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT. fmt, clippy -D warnings (default and --features cuda), 2972 workspace tests, xtask verify-architecture pass.

LRU model eviction under VRAM pressure. Verified live on the CUDA release daemon (8 GB card): with 0.5B, 1.5B and 3B loaded fully on GPU (3994 MiB used) and 0.5B touched last, loading qwen2.5-coder-7b evicted 1.5B then 3B in LRU order (re-measuring free VRAM after each), kept the most-recent 0.5B, and the 7B landed 28/28 layers on GPU — previously 25/28 when the daemon held its auto-loaded models. Unit tests cover the eviction plan (no eviction when it fits, LRU until it fits, evict-all when short) and idle_lru ordering (skips in-use and excluded entries). fmt, clippy -D warnings (default and --features cuda), 2975 workspace tests, xtask verify-architecture pass.

Host-state integrity hardening (commits 4ea83f96..ff7537f9). (1) One race-safe writer: susi_config::atomic_write_bytes (unique dot-prefixed create_new staging, fsync, rename) replaces ~25 fixed-name '.tmp' / per-process-name writers across gemi-models, agents, core (broker, commit log, plane bus, intent bus, registry, grants, capture, service table, net guard), tools, sandbox, cluster key, quarantine, and root peers CLI. (2) One secret loader: susi_config::load_or_create_secret (no-replace hard link, strict 32-byte length, entropy failure is an error) now backs the audit-chain key and the MAC-policy key; the daemon's duplicate MAC loader is gone (wire_mac_policy delegates to MacPolicy::wired, which fails closed to local_only when the key is unavailable). Plane-bus secret and grant-audit key no longer become all-zero on entropy failure. (3) One credential redactor: susi_config::redact_credentials (env *_API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET values + governance.secret_tokens, bundled fallback) replaces five drifted redactors; the audit-log chokepoint, capture, and SecurityDetector no longer fail open on config errors; Google 'AIza' keys were previously unredacted by all ad-hoc redactors. (4) Vendored sandbox runtime shares manager/runtime_shared.rs with the service runtime (had drifted). catalog_store.rs removed — supersedes the file anchor in the 2026-09-22 Phase 1 optimization entry. SUSI OS hardening steps 75-90 (commits 944b3815..c500f943). Network availability: streamable-HTTP MCP connect is bounded; plane-bus, GEMI REST, and GMCP connections are capped; silent transport handshakes and slow request headers time out; the shared bounded HTTP builder serves normal traffic. Process lifecycle: timed-out peer CLIs, readiness probes, hardware/host observations, and cancelled exec_command children are killed and reaped with stdin closed. Policy and truthfulness: IDENTITY describes EvolutionManager as an observer rather than a self-healing writer; exec_command confines paths embedded in option values; local_only explicitly gates every egress-capable tool. Configuration safety: overflowing waits cannot abort the daemon and GMCP permits are clamped. Remote-input memory is bounded for cloud inference, catalogs, Ollama tags, and live search. Placement decisions can be resolved by authenticated id to their signed audit record. Finally, audit-chain appends use the shared cross-process FileLock, preventing concurrent CLI/daemon writers from forking the chain or interleaving JSON. Regression coverage includes silent clients, the bounded connection builder, surviving-child detection, option-path escapes, all egress tools, placement lookup, and a four-process audit append race.

entries.milestone: Identity and public-contract reconciliation after the 100-step SUSI OS hardening sequence. README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md now define one governed operating layer across local AI (models/runtimes/GPU lifecycle/MCP/Wasm/workspace agents) and explicitly configured cloud AI (providers/MCP/A2A/managed peers), document the shared placement/evidence/audit/privacy contracts, expose placement-id correlation and authenticated audit lookup, and state the crash-safe audit invariants. identity.json removes the remaining false EvolutionAgent self-healing claim, describes the implemented local/cloud placement plane, receipt generations, and fail-closed cross-process audit chain. VISION.md is explicitly target-state rather than evidence, and roadmap metadata now targets the next 0.15.0 line with Local + Cloud Federation as the strategic priority.

VISION.md corrected from a mixed list of present-tense implementation claims, unverified scale/latency promises, business outcomes, and aspirational recognition into an actionable local-and-cloud AI operating-layer vision. The new document separates direction from current truth, defines the local, cloud, and shared decision planes; states the swarm and trust boundaries; summarizes the evidence-backed baseline with explicit source-of-truth links; sets the 0.15 placement/federation/evidence/ecosystem horizon; adds release gates and non-goals; and forbids unsupported scale, uptime, compliance, adoption, and impact claims. Stale source comments tied to deleted vision bullet numbers were replaced with descriptive contracts, including removal of an unmeasured 10k-cell sub-millisecond scheduler assertion.

RSI iteration 1/100: automatic reflex distillation now fails closed. The audit previously treated unreadable staged data and global-config errors as empty/default state, returned training failures inside an Ok string, and ignored failure to delete consumed samples. It now distinguishes absent staging from unreadable staging, propagates configuration and training errors as typed EaiError values, and surfaces sample-retirement failure. Regression tests cover absent, populated including unterminated-final-line, and unreadable staging. Targeted fmt, test, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 2/100: native reflex training is now cumulative and single-writer. The prior implementation initialized a fresh random VarMap for every run, trained it, and replaced the previous weights, so repeated distillation did not improve the existing model. It now acquires a cross-process reflex-training lock, resolves configuration without a silent default, creates the model directory explicitly, loads published weights into the trainable variables when present, then atomically renames the trained checkpoint. Existing but unreadable/incompatible weights abort training instead of being silently discarded. The result text now accurately says native cumulative training rather than autonomous evolution. Targeted fmt, test, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 3/100: automatic and forced reflex training now consume the experience buffer that SUSI actually writes. ProtocolKnowledgeBase stages pairs at <workspace>/.susi/distillation_staged.jsonl, but ReflexTrainer ignored its workspace argument and looked only in the host config directory; therefore normal workspace experience could never trigger or feed training. SusiAlphaModel now separates the globally published model directory from an explicit staged-data path, while the existing global-buffer entry point remains as a compatibility wrapper. ReflexTrainer uses the invoking workspace buffer for thresholding, training, and post-success retirement, while retaining the globally shared weights and cross-process training lock. Targeted fmt, test, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 4/100: reflex training corpus validation now fails closed before tensor construction or checkpoint publication. Previously malformed JSONL records were silently skipped, empty corpora still trained on synthetic seeds, and unknown action text was assigned to the lexicographically last dynamic intent, poisoning the classifier with fabricated labels. Every record must now be valid JSON, carry a non-empty intent, and name one exact registered action case-insensitively; malformed, blank, empty, and unknown-action corpora return an error and remain staged for diagnosis. Regression tests prove malformed records retain line attribution, substring guesses are rejected, and canonical case-insensitive actions map to the correct label. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 5/100: reflex-label provenance now comes from successful execution receipts rather than model answer prose. The previous consolidator copied memory.jsonl outcome text into the action field, even though outcomes are free-form answers and no downstream evidence proves they name an executed action; the classifier therefore learned fabricated labels (or, after iteration 4, rejected every such record). Consolidation now reads the append-only receipt archive, stages only successful records with non-empty mission_goal and tool fields, uses the receipt's tool as the canonical action, and preserves receipt_id/output_hash provenance in metadata. Malformed archive records fail closed with a line number. A regression test proves a successful list_directory receipt is staged with provenance while an unsuccessful write_file receipt is excluded. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 6/100: corrected iteration 5's incomplete intent provenance after auditing the real ArchivedReceipt schema. Receipt archives stored only mission_goal_hash, so a consolidator expecting mission_goal text could never stage production data. EvidenceSession now supplies its credential-redacted mission text to ReceiptArchive alongside the unchanged hash of the original goal; ArchivedReceipt carries it as an additive optional training_intent so legacy v1 lines remain readable. PKB consolidation uses ReceiptArchive::load_audit_lines rather than reading only the live file, covering all retained generations, and excludes legacy records that cannot prove their training intent. Tests verify the capture boundary persists the redacted training intent, successful receipt pairing, unsuccessful exclusion, and safe legacy-record handling. This entry explicitly supersedes EV-2022927-171's unsupported implication that the pre-existing receipt schema contained mission_goal text. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 7/100: receipt-backed training ingestion is now event-driven and non-replaying. Periodic consolidation reread every retained receipt on every daemon cycle, amplifying old examples and requiring another cursor ledger. The duplicate scan path is removed: after a successful receipt archive append, that same capture operation stages exactly one complete JSONL training record under a dedicated cross-process lock; unsuccessful receipts, empty intents, and empty tool names do not stage. The record carries the redacted live mission, executed tool, receipt id, and output hash. PKB retains only its explicit staging API; daemon consolidation no longer scans history. The receipt-capture regression test proves the archive and one matching staged sample are produced together. This supersedes EV-2022927-172's retained-generation consolidation design while preserving its redacted intent field for audit. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 8/100: neural reflex output labels now have a stable persisted vocabulary. Previously training and prediction each rebuilt and sorted the live agent/tool registry, so adding a capability could shift existing indices and reinterpret learned weights as different actions. SusiAlphaModel now stores its validated action vocabulary beside the weights, loads that exact mapping for inference and cumulative training, appends newly discovered capabilities without reordering existing labels, rejects missing/corrupt/duplicate/oversized vocabularies for published weights, and restricts prediction to mapped output slots. Fresh models persist weights and vocabulary together; model/config read and initialization failures are no longer silently replaced with random published state. Regression tests prove extension preserves existing indices and case-insensitive duplicates fail validation. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 9/100: persisted reflex action labels are now cryptographically bound to the exact checkpoint they interpret. A separate weights rename and vocabulary write could previously leave a crash-mixed pair that loaded successfully but mapped output indices through the wrong labels. The vocabulary sidecar now has a strict versioned schema and the SHA-256 of the published safetensors file; every inference and cumulative-training load recomputes and compares that digest before accepting the mapping. Unknown schema, malformed sidecar, invalid labels, or weight mismatch fails closed. A regression test writes a valid pair, proves it loads, mutates only the weights, and proves mismatch rejection. This establishes detection; automatic last-known-good recovery is a separate subsequent iteration. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 10/100: reflex checkpoint publication is now crash-safe as a bundle. In-place weights replacement followed by vocabulary replacement had a detectable but unrecoverable mixed-pair window. Training and fresh initialization now write an immutable generation-specific safetensors file and its hash-bound vocabulary first, then atomically publish a small versioned manifest naming that generation. Readers resolve only the manifest's same-directory filename and reject traversal, unsupported schema, missing checkpoint, corrupt vocabulary, or digest mismatch; a crash before the manifest update leaves the prior generation active. Legacy configured weight files remain readable and migrate on the next successful training publication. Cache fingerprinting follows the manifest rather than a legacy filename. Regression coverage proves valid local resolution and traversal rejection. Generation retention cleanup remains a later lifecycle iteration; correctness no longer depends on it. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 11/100: reflex bundles now retain and recover from one last-known-good generation. Each publication records the previously validated checkpoint in the atomic manifest. Inference validates active vocabulary/hash/safetensors construction first and automatically tries previous on any active failure; cumulative training selects the first hash-valid active-or-previous source instead of becoming permanently wedged by a damaged active file. Both manifest paths are constrained to local filenames. A regression test creates a corrupt active generation and valid hash-bound previous generation and proves usable_checkpoint selects the previous mapping. This converts iteration 9's detection and iteration 10's crash-safe pointer into an operational recovery path. Retention cleanup of generations older than active+previous remains the next lifecycle concern. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 12/100: immutable reflex checkpoint generations now have bounded lifecycle retention. After the new manifest is durably published, SUSI preserves exactly the active and last-known-good checkpoint pairs and removes only generation files matching its strict <stem>.<u128-generation>.<u32-pid>.safetensors naming scheme plus their vocabulary sidecars; legacy configured weights and unrelated similarly named files are not candidates. Cleanup runs only after pointer publication, so failure cannot invalidate the active bundle, and any removal failures are surfaced in the successful training report as cleanup warnings rather than falsely turning a completed model publication into a failed training transaction. Regression coverage proves active/previous and unrelated files survive while an older generated pair is removed. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 13/100: reflex training no longer loses receipts captured during a training run. The trainer previously read the live workspace JSONL and deleted that same path after training, racing receipt capture; any append between read and delete vanished unlearned. Automatic and forced training now acquire the producer's cross-process staging lock, atomically rename the eligible buffer into a unique claim workspace, release the lock so capture immediately continues into a new live file, and train only the immutable claim. Success retires only the claim. Failure reacquires the lock and atomically restores claimed bytes before any newly captured bytes, preserving both ordering and data. Tests prove concurrent post-claim samples survive successful retirement and failed training restoration produces old-then-new records with no residual claim directory. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 14/100: crash-stranded reflex training claims now recover deterministically. Automatic and forced training hold a workspace-wide cross-process training-cycle lease from recovery through claim retirement, preventing another process from mistaking a live claim for an orphan; the existing PID-aware FileLock reclaims the lease after process death. Before each cycle, SUSI finds only strictly named reflex-claim-<u128-generation>-<u32-pid> directories, orders them by generation, merges their complete bytes ahead of the current live staging buffer under the producer lock, atomically publishes the restored buffer, and removes recovered claim directories. Unrelated directories are untouched and read/write/removal failures surface. A regression test proves two out-of-order orphan directories recover oldest-first before live samples and are retired. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 15/100: learning ingestion is now observable instead of best-effort and silent. Each archived receipt records whether its training sample was actually persisted to the staging buffer: `training_staged` is `Some(true)` when the sample was durably written, `Some(false)` when staging failed (lock acquisition, file open, or write), and `None` when no staging was attempted (unsuccessful receipt or empty intent/action). Failures now emit a typed `EaiError::io` that enters the `error_metrics.jsonl` sink instead of disappearing. The `ArchivedReceipt` field is additive with `#[serde(default)]` so older v1 records without it deserialize as `None`. Regression coverage proves: successful staging records `true`, unsuccessful receipts record `None` with no staging file, staging blocked by a directory-in-place records `false`, and v1 records without the field deserialize correctly. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 16/100: autonomous drift audits now report staging health. ReceiptArchive::staging_health_summary aggregates training_staged into staged-ok, failed, and not-attempted counts across the receipt archive, and EvolutionManager::perform_autonomous_drift_audit appends that one-line summary. Operators see systemic ingestion failures without scanning error_metrics.jsonl. StagingHealth is exported from susi-core and the embedded vendored surface. A regression test aggregates successful and unsuccessful receipts. This entry was recorded with iteration 18 because the producing commit landed without an evidence row. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 17/100: every reflex training report includes staging health. Both audit_distillation_state and force_train append the same one-line staging summary as the drift audit, including the idle path where the sample threshold was not met. Operators see whether capture succeeded next to the training outcome. This entry was recorded with iteration 18 because the producing commit landed without an evidence row. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 18/100: a torn or blank line in a claimed training buffer no longer rejects the batch or inflates the threshold. After the atomic claim rename, SUSI keeps only complete JSON lines, records each drop through EaiError::io, and rewrites the claim. Survivors below the threshold are restored to the live buffer; a claim with nothing usable left is retired and the cycle stays idle instead of training a deleted file. Regression tests cover a torn tail plus a blank line, a below-threshold restore, and an all-malformed claim that leaves no reflex-claim directory. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 19/100: one untrainable record no longer stalls reflex training. parse_training_entries still refuses to guess labels, but a well-formed record with a blank intent or an action outside the reflex vocabulary is now skipped and counted instead of failing the whole batch. Previously the reflex trainer restored the failed claim, so the same batch failed every cycle, and once the vocabulary reached its DIM cap an unknown action could never become trainable. Skips are recorded through EaiError::inference and reported in the training result; malformed or blank lines still fail loudly, and a batch with no trainable records still errors. A regression test mixes known, unknown-action, blank-intent, and case-variant records and proves a torn line still fails. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 20/100: a Tier-0 reflex failure no longer masquerades as a solved answer. When the neural classifier, generative reflex, and local full-answer tiers all failed, SusiPulse::reason returned Ok("I'm unable to generate an answer at this time.") and cached it; ReflexEngine::try_solve then reported ReflexDecision::Solved, so GemiRuntime::reason_internal returned the apology and never reached cloud escalation or discovered providers, and the cached apology outlived the transient failure until the weights changed. reason() now returns Err when no tier answers (never cached), and try_generate_answer fails its task and returns Err on an empty decode instead of the same placeholder. The reflex cache is also keyed by workspace (a list_directory reflex embeds the workspace path and was served across workspaces) and bounded at 1024 entries in the long-lived daemon. Unit tests cover the bound and workspace separation; cargo test -p susi-gemi pulse and cargo clippy -p susi-gemi --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 21/100: the Tier-0 reflex hot path stops reloading the published model per prompt, and a dead public surface is removed. SusiPulse::reason called SusiAlphaModel::load for every uncached prompt, re-reading the config, resolving the bundle manifest, re-hashing the vocabulary binding, and re-mmapping the weights against the sub-2ms reflex mandate. Meanwhile SusiAlphaModel::global() had no callers (a dead pub surface carrying two unwrap allowances) and was a OnceLock that could never observe new weights. global() is replaced by SusiAlphaModel::cached, which reuses the loaded model until the bundle fingerprint changes and caches only when the fingerprint read before and after the load match and are stable, so a publication that races the load (including the bootstrap bundle load itself publishes) can never pin an older model under a newer fingerprint. A unit test proves the bootstrap load is not cached, the next load is, and repeated calls share one Arc. cargo test -p susi-gemi alpha and cargo clippy -p susi-gemi --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 22/100: the self-patch cycle is all-or-nothing. apply_patch_cycle wrote files one at a time and returned Err on a stale later file or an unspawnable test command without restoring the files it had already written, leaving a half-applied patch; an empty old text silently overwrote an existing file despite the code's own create-only comment; restore errors were discarded and still reported reverted=true; and it kept a second rollback path (in-memory map plus write-only .susi/patch_backups copies that collided on same-named files) beside the TxManager transaction that already snapshotted the same files. Every file is now checked for staleness before any write, TxManager is the single rollback source (begin failure is an error, not .ok()), write and spawn failures abort the transaction, and a failed rollback is reported as ROLLBACK FAILED instead of reverted. Regression tests cover a stale second file leaving the first untouched, empty old refusing to clobber, and a created file removed after a failing test. cargo test -p susi-gawd patch_cycle (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-gawd --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 23/100: the swarm task table no longer shows phantom Running tasks. A TaskHandle released without mark_completed/mark_failed (an owner returning early through ?, e.g. GenerativeReflexEngine::try_solve/try_generate_answer when the reflex model or tokenizer is not provisioned, or ModelManager's foreground install on artifact_name failure) left its record Running forever, and categories with fewer than three calibrated samples are never reaped by the idle watchdog, so glass-box task listings reported work that had already ended. TaskHandle now implements Drop: a handle released while still Running or Paused finishes as Failed with an [ABANDONED] result. finish() is first-writer-wins, so an explicit outcome, a kill, or a watchdog stall is never overwritten, and background downloads that hold an Arc clone are unaffected until the last clone drops. A unit test proves a dropped live handle is recorded as abandoned and an explicitly failed handle keeps its real error. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (5 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 24/100: the daemon's swarm task table is bounded. SwarmTaskManager never removed a record, so every neural inference, reflex call, model download, exec_command, and fleet agent dispatch added one TaskRecord plus a cancel flag and a pause flag for the life of the process, and every list_tasks payload grew with them. register_task now prunes the oldest finished (Completed/Failed/Stalled/Killed) records once the table reaches 512, removing their cancel and pause entries too; Running and Paused tasks are never evicted. A unit test registers 1024 finished tasks beside one live task and proves the table stays within the bound, the three maps stay in step, and the live task survives. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (6 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 25/100: the Mandate 32 idle lease is actually calibrated from observation. get_idle_threshold_ms documents a lease of 5x the worst observed idle gap per category, but TaskHandle::mark_completed always passed a hard-coded 100 ms as max_observed_idle_ms, so every calibrated category's p99_idle_interval_ms was the 200 ms floor and the lease collapsed to the operator floor whatever the real workload did. A slow category (e.g. model_download between chunk callbacks, or neural_inference prefill before its first token) was never learned.
