TaskHandle now records milliseconds since start of each progress report and folds every gap (start to first report, report to report, last report to completion) into max_idle_ms, which mark_completed passes to the telemetry store. Known limitation, stated rather than hidden: time a task spends paused is counted as idle, which can only loosen, never tighten, the learned lease. A unit test sleeps 60 ms between reports and proves the measured gap is at least 60 ms. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 26/100: learned idle-lease calibration survives crashes. TelemetryHistoryStore::save_history rewrote data_dir/telemetry_history.json with a plain std::fs::write after every completed task and discarded the error; a crash or concurrent writer mid-write left a torn file, and load_history silently ignored the parse failure, so every category restarted uncalibrated with no signal that learned leases had been lost. save_history now serializes and writes through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes (staged file, fsync, rename), and read, parse, and write failures are recorded through EaiError::io instead of being swallowed. Known limitation, stated: two processes still last-writer-win on the whole map (no merge). cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 27/100: compacting the context graph can no longer destroy it, and sibling processes stay in sync across compaction. ContextGraph::persist (run by compact, compact_if_large at attach, and append_event once the log passes 16 MiB) opened the log with truncate(true) and rewrote it line by line, so a crash or kill mid-rewrite left an empty or partial log and the next start replayed only that remnant. Separately, replay resumed a sibling's cursor whenever the file had not shrunk, so after another process compacted and the log regrew past the cursor, replay started mid-line and silently skipped the first records. persist now serializes into a buffer and replaces the log through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes, recording the new file's (device, inode) under the context_graph lock; replay compares the open file's identity (unix) with the one its cursor belongs to and refolds from zero when the log was replaced (the size check remains the non-unix fallback). A regression test replaces the log by rename with a longer file and proves both records are folded; the existing persist/replay, compaction, torn-tail, and capacity tests still pass (cargo test -p susi-core context_graph: 9 passed). cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 28/100: a full context graph no longer pays a full-table sort on every insert. enforce_capacity evicted exactly down to the 32,000-node cap, so once the graph was full every record_node (every recorded tool call, observation, telemetry snapshot, and patch cycle) cloned all 32k node ids, sorted them, and evicted a single victim, a per-insert O(n log n) cost on the hot path. Crossing the cap now evicts down to a low-water mark of 30,000 (1/16 headroom), so that sort is amortized over about 2,000 inserts; victim selection is unchanged (oldest ephemeral first, then oldest overall, ties by id) and edges of evicted nodes are still removed. The capacity test now proves eviction lands on the low-water mark, still spares the older structural node and removes the victim's edge, and that the next insert below the cap does not evict again. cargo test -p susi-core context_graph (9 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 29/100: a hung agent command can finally be reaped by the idle-lease watchdog. exec_command's wait loop called task_handle.report_progress() every 50 ms whether or not the child produced anything, so a silent, wedged command (a blocked network call, a prompt waiting on /dev/null, a deadlocked build) always looked busy: the Mandate 32 watchdog never saw it idle, and the exec_command category's learned lease was calibrated to about 50 ms regardless of the real workload. Progress is now reported only by the pipe drains, once per chunk the child actually writes (drain_exec_pipe, extracted to module level); the wait loop only polls. A try_wait error now kills and reaps the child and fails the task instead of looping forever. Known limitation, stated: a legitimately silent long command is now subject to the calibrated lease, floored by the operator's execution_lease_secs and not applied before three completed samples. A unit test proves an empty pipe reports no progress and a pipe with output does. Also verified this session: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean and a full cargo test --workspace run with no failures (after fixing the iteration-27 test's tempfile use, see commit e64bd5ad).

RSI iteration 30/100: a crash during first start can no longer strand a node outside its cluster. cluster_key() and node_id() created ~/.susi/cluster.key and ~/.susi/node_id with create_new(0600) and then a separate write_all. A crash or kill between the two left an empty file; cluster_key then logged it as malformed and refused to auto-rotate on every call, leaving the node in unsigned mode (peers can never reach Explicit), and node_id's create_new kept failing on the existing file, so the host advertised a new ephemeral identity each process and lost its stable coordinator identity. A concurrent first start (daemon plus CLI) could also read the empty file mid-creation. Both now create through the existing susi_config::install_private_file (written in full to a 0600 staging file, then hard-linked into place, so readers never see a partial file and a racing creator never overwrites the winner), and a whitespace-only file is treated as a torn creation, cleared under a file lock, and reinstalled. A malformed non-empty key is still never auto-rotated. install_private_file is now also re-exported from susi-config (it already was from susi-core's mount), with no second writer added. A new test proves an empty cluster.key and node_id are regenerated and then persist, the key is 0600, and a malformed non-empty key still yields None; cargo test -p susi-config cluster_key (9 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 31/100: the daemon binary trust anchor is always a digest of the whole binary and is replaced atomically. calculate_binary_hash looped on while let Ok(n) = file.read(..), so any read error (EINTR included) silently ended the loop and returned the SHA-256 of a truncated prefix as if it were the binary's hash. ensure_daemon_running then cached that digest in binary.hash.cache under the binary's mtime and size and wrote it as the binary.hash trust anchor, triggering a spurious 'binary recompiled' daemon restart, and is_trusted_susi_process (which re-hashes /proc/<pid>/exe uncached) would then stop recognizing the genuine daemon. Both files were also written with a plain fs::write whose errors were ignored, so a torn binary.hash reported a phantom recompile on the next CLI call. The hash now retries Interrupted and returns every other read error; binary.hash is replaced through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes and a failed anchor write is returned (the daemon logs it as an unverifiable check instead of claiming success); the cache is also written atomically, best effort. A unit test hashes a 200 KB file spanning several reads against a reference digest, proves the anchor is established, a rebuild reports false once and is then trusted, and a missing binary is an error. cargo test -p susi-sandbox daemon_state and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass (daemon_state.rs is path-mounted into susi-tools, susi-server, and susi-agents; all compile).

RSI iteration 32/100: agent transactions can no longer overwrite each other's rollback snapshots, and their durable state is honest. TxManager minted ids tx-N from a per-process counter and wrote the snapshot to <workspace>/.susi/tx/tx-N.json with an unchecked fs::write. A process that had not called hydrate (the daemon's patch cycle, a swarm plan transaction, an MCP tx_begin) started again at tx-1 and overwrote an earlier transaction's file, including an Open one whose snapshot was the only way for a later process to roll it back. begin also reported success when the durable copy was never written, and commit/abort ignored their persist failures, so a committed transaction could remain Open on disk and be rolled back by a later process. Ids are now reserved on disk with create_new (retrying on AlreadyExists), every persist replaces the file through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes, and begin, commit, and abort return persist failures. The unused TxManager::track_file (no callers; it snapshotted unreadable files as empty content, which an abort would have written back over the real file) is removed as a dead pub surface. A regression test runs begin from two fresh managers on one workspace, proves distinct ids, that the first snapshot survives on disk, and that a third, hydrated manager can still abort the first transaction and restore the file. cargo test -p susi-core agent_tx (3 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 33/100: the autonomous planner stops claiming a rollback it never performed (Mandate 1). solve_autonomous opened a TxManager transaction for the whole plan with an empty file list, so it snapshotted nothing; when a step failed it aborted that empty transaction and reported 'Autonomous plan aborted at step N (transaction rolled back)', while every file earlier steps had written through agents and tools stayed changed. A step returning Err through ? also left the transaction Open in .susi/tx forever. The no-op transaction is removed, and the failure report now states that workspace changes made by earlier steps were not rolled back. A real plan-wide rollback would need every agent write routed through a tracked snapshot; that is not claimed. ARCHITECTURE.md's planning-loop row now says the same. cargo clippy -p susi-gawd-swarm --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 34/100: transactions close only against their own workspace, and the MCP surface can close transactions other processes began. TxManager::abort restored each snapshot by joining its relative path onto whatever workspace the caller passed, not the one it snapshotted, so tx_abort (MCP) or susi tx abort run from another project would write the first project's file contents into the second. Ids are reserved per workspace journal (iteration 32), so the same id can name different transactions in different workspaces. Separately, the MCP tx_commit and tx_abort tools never hydrated the durable .susi/tx journal, so the daemon answered 'unknown tx' for any transaction begun by susi tx begin in a CLI process. commit and abort now refuse, with a governance error, a workspace that does not canonicalize to the transaction's own (commit gained a workspace parameter; patch_cycle and the CLI pass theirs), and tx_commit/tx_abort hydrate the workspace journal first. A regression test proves abort and commit from another workspace are refused and leave its file untouched, and the owning workspace can still abort. cargo test -p susi-core agent_tx (4 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 35/100: a phantom Tier-2 reasoning model is removed from the code and the constitution. susi_gemi::reasoning::SusiReasoningModel (a four-layer Candle MLP loading models/susi-reason.safetensors) had no caller anywhere in the workspace, its missing-weights error told users to run 'susi train_reason', a command that does not exist, and nothing in the tree ever wrote those weights. identity.json nevertheless listed it in Pillar II as the component NativeReasoningModel, 'Distilled Tier 2 logic weights'. The module, its duplicate ReasoningSample type, the reasoning re-export, and the NativeReasoningModel component row are removed; deep reasoning is what it already was in practice, routed to real local (GGUF/Ollama/vLLM) or cloud LLMs by GemiRuntime. Verified before removal: a repo-wide search found no use of SusiReasoningModel, susi_gemi::reasoning, train_reason, or susi-reason.safetensors outside the deleted file and the identity row. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 36/100: the constitution's component table no longer lists components that do not exist. Pillar II still carried SUSI-Vision and SUSI-Audio rows ('Candle-based image/audio-feature extractor (untrained linear projection)') although commit 1d9c616f removed that multimodal code and 6a0fac47 dropped its roadmap vector; a repo-wide search finds no vision or audio extractor in crates/ or src/. Both rows are removed. The UniversalExecutionSubstrate row named no symbol and claimed support for 'multiple model formats'; it is renamed to the real symbol InferenceHost and now states what runtime_substrate.rs loads natively (GGUF llama/qwen2 with a GPU layer split) and that other formats are reached only through HTTP providers. Method: every component symbol was grepped as a whole word across crates/ and src/; the remaining zero-hit rows (SUSI-Alpha, NativeAlphaModel, ExternalAgentManager) are display names for real code (SusiAlphaModel, the susi-alpha weights, susi_agents::external::AgentManager) and are kept.

RSI iteration 37/100: a damaged ban list can no longer readmit evicted cluster members or erase earlier bans. peers_banned.json was parsed in five places (swarm handshake admission in amas and the daemon's UDP responder via peer_registry::is_banned, roster pruning, net_guard's peer-bearer check, the MCP member-proposal intake, and the commit-log membership apply), each with read_to_string(..).ok().and_then(parse).unwrap_or_default(), so a torn, corrupt, or unreadable ban list read as empty and every evicted member passed admission again. The commit-log apply then rewrote that empty view plus one new ban over the damaged file on the next committed removal, permanently erasing all earlier bans. One fail-closed check now lives in susi_config::cluster_key (mounted by every crate): config_json_rows_checked_at distinguishes absent (empty) from damaged (Err), and member_banned/member_banned_at treat a damaged list as banned; all four admission paths use it with the shared ban_row_matches rule. The commit-log apply reads the list uncached and strictly, and skips membership application entirely (no roster change, no rewrite) while it is damaged. peer_registry's unused ban_peer/ban_peer_at, BannedPeer, load_banned_peers(_from) and is_banned_in (no callers outside their own test) are removed. Tests: damaged_ban_list_fails_closed (absent, matching by id or address, corrupt list counts as banned) and an extension of member_records_seal_verify_and_apply_to_roster proving a committed removal leaves a corrupt list byte-identical and a committed add leaves peers.json unchanged. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm peer_registry, -p susi-core commit_log (15 passed) and net_guard, -p susi-config, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 38/100: the verified-peer roster can no longer be erased by one persist. persist_verified_peer_to (called on every successful signed handshake) loaded peers.json through serde_json::from_str::<Vec<ClusterPeerNode>>(..).unwrap_or_default(), so a torn file, or a single row another writer shaped without one of ClusterPeerNode's nine required fields, made the whole array read as empty; it then atomically rewrote the file with just the peer it was admitting, erasing every other verified member. The commit-log membership apply had the same read-as-empty-then-rewrite shape for peers.json. susi_config::cluster_key::read_json_rows_strict now provides one uncached strict reader (absent is empty, damaged is Err), shared by config_json_rows_checked_at and the commit-log apply (which now reads both files through it and skips while either is damaged). persist_verified_peer_to edits JSON rows in place, keeping explicit rows it cannot type-parse, and refuses to rewrite a damaged roster; load_persisted_peers_from parses row by row so one foreign row no longer hides every typed peer. The two path-seam functions now take &Path. A regression test persists beside a minimally shaped explicit row and proves both rows remain on disk while the typed loader still returns the typed peer, and that a damaged roster is left byte-identical. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm peer_registry (4 passed), -p susi-core commit_log (15 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 39/100: the error-metrics sink no longer records credentials (Mandate 10). Every EaiError constructor appends {error: self.to_string(), ...} to data_dir/error_metrics.jsonl (or posts it to the susi-error service), and that text routinely embeds command stderr (exec_command fails with the child's stderr), remote URLs with basic-auth tokens, and provider error bodies. Nothing redacted it, although susi_config::redact_credentials exists for exactly this class of text; the error contract sits below the config crate in the leaf order and could not call it. The contract now masks error text before recording: environment credentials (*_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET values, 8+ chars) via a new pure susi_error::redact::mask_env_credentials, which redact_credentials now reuses instead of keeping its own copy, then the governance.secret_tokens list embedded at build time from config/config.default.json, so the default list has one source. Known limitation, stated: operator-added patterns in the host config are not applied at this layer (the contract cannot load config); redact_credentials still applies them at the trust-boundary surfaces it guards. A test proves the bundled list is embedded and that a ghp_ token in a remote URL and an sk- key are masked while the message survives. cargo test -p susi-error metrics_redaction and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass (contract.rs and redact.rs are path-mounted into every crate).

RSI iteration 40/100: every error writer now reaches the same metrics file in the same way. The susi-error service (lib.rs) and the vendored contract mounted in 14 crates (susi-core/src/susi_error.rs) each carried their own copy of the rotate-then-append logic and their own data-dir resolver. The vendored resolver hard-coded ~/.local/share/susi and ignored SUSI_HOME, and the service's used directories::ProjectDirs and also ignored SUSI_HOME, so a sibling instance's errors landed in the default instance's metrics file and, on non-Linux XDG hosts, the service and the local fallbacks wrote different files. The service also wrote each record with writeln!, which can split one record across several write calls, and neither copy restricted the file's mode. A shared sink.rs (path-mounted by both, like contract.rs and redact.rs) now owns the cap and rotation, emits each record in a single write_all on an O_APPEND handle, and creates the file 0600 on Unix. Both paths resolve the file through the vendored susi_paths::SusiDirs client every other crate uses (service-backed, SUSI_HOME-aware; susi-error and susi-native now mount it), keeping susi-error at zero SUSI Cargo dependencies as tests/architecture_tests.rs requires (a first attempt with a direct susi-paths dependency failed that test and was reverted; the directories dependency is dropped). POST /log_error now also masks posted text with redact_for_metrics, since any local client can post. A test proves two records append as whole lines to an owner-only file. cargo test -p susi-error (10 passed), --test architecture_tests (17 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 41/100: a damaged privacy posture now fails closed instead of downgrading a local_only host. Every wired MacPolicy copy (daemon plus the vendored susi_core in each leaf crate) re-reads substrate_home/privacy_mode on each mode() call, and parsed it with the lenient PrivacyMode::parse, which maps anything unrecognized (an empty file, a torn write, garbage) to Balanced. Balanced makes blocks_cloud_inference false and drops mandatory_sandbox, so a local_only host silently re-enabled cloud inference and unsandboxed host exec. MacPolicy::set_mode also rewrote that file with a plain, error-ignoring std::fs::write, right after persist_privacy_mode had written it atomically, which reopened exactly the torn-read window persist_privacy_mode's own comment guards against, and a failed write still reported a switch other processes never saw. The sticky file is now parsed exactly (PrivacyMode::parse_persisted); unrecognized or unreadable content enforces LocalOnly with an error log, and absence still means no override. set_mode is the single atomic writer for wired policies and returns io::Result; persist_privacy_mode delegates to it, writing directly only when the global policy is unwired (substrate key unavailable, forced local_only) so the choice still persists for the next boot. A test covers absent, each valid mode, and empty or partial content failing closed, plus an atomic set_mode round-trip. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (8 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 42/100: scoped capability grants stop at a path or host boundary. MacPolicy::is_permitted (and its persisted-grant scan) accepted any grant whose resource was a raw string prefix of the request, and the daemon's syscall CapabilityPolicy did the same for scoped grants (workspace.starts_with(scope)). A cell granted filesystem.read on a canonical workspace /srv/ws was therefore authorized for /srv/ws2 and /srv/ws-secrets, and a grant on https://api.example.com also covered https://api.example.com.evil.net. Confirmed by a failing test before the fix. One rule, mac_policy::grant_covers, now decides coverage: exact match; an explicit trailing * globs its prefix (the default app://* transmit grant keeps working); otherwise the request must sit under the grant at a / boundary. Both the in-memory and persisted MAC lookups and the daemon's scope_matches use it (no second copy). Tests: scoped_grants_stop_at_a_path_or_host_boundary (path child allowed, sibling paths denied, URL child allowed, look-alike host denied, glob allowed within its scheme only) and a sibling-path case added to the daemon's scoped_grant_restricts_workspace. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (9 passed) and abi_bridge (9 passed), -p susi-daemon security (8 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 43/100: the agent-to-agent broker tool ipc_send is reachable again. requirements_for_tool demanded (transmit, "*") for ipc_send*, but the only transmit grant the policy ever issues is the default (susi, transmit, app://*); the exact-key lookup, the * wildcard lookup, and the scoped match all miss that pair, so authorize_tool returned 'MAC DENY: subject susi lacks transmit on *' in balanced, local_only, and open modes alike, and every MCP/registry call of ipc_send (wrapped by EnforcedTool) failed before IpcBroker's own per-sender dispatch grant was consulted. Confirmed with a failing test in all three modes before the change. ipc_send now requires transmit on app://*, the local-delivery scope the default grant covers; IpcBroker still enforces its dispatch grant per sender. A regression test authorizes ipc_send under all three modes. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (10 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 44/100: admitting an MCP server can no longer erase the rest of mcp_config.json. auto_configure_server and admit_mcp_server both loaded the file with serde_json::from_str().unwrap_or(empty) (and treated any read error as empty), then atomically wrote the result back. A torn file, or a file that could not be read, therefore became a config containing only the server being added. read_mcp_config now treats NotFound as an empty config and returns ERROR_CONFIG_DAMAGED or ERROR_CONFIG_UNREADABLE without writing. Regression tests prove a torn file is left byte-identical by both writers, and a directory standing in for the file is not replaced. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 45/100: model downloads are verified against the publisher's SHA-256, and the README no longer overclaims. README said 'Binaries and model weights are checksum-verified', but install.sh downloads no weights, download::transfer only validated a finished artifact structurally (GGUF magic, tokenizer parse, non-empty), and nothing ever wrote the ModelProvenance.original_checksum that verify_model_integrity checks on every cold load, so that tamper check never ran for anything SUSI downloaded. Verified live against huggingface.co this session: a resolve URL answers 302 with x-linked-etag set to the file's quoted 64-hex SHA-256 and x-linked-size, and the redirect-following reqwest client never saw those headers. download::published_sha256 now asks once per install with a non-redirecting HEAD; transfer takes the expected digest and, via a single publish() helper used by both the normal and the 416-already-complete paths, hashes the validated part (reusing ModelManager::calculate_simple_checksum), discards it on mismatch so the next attempt restarts clean, and on success writes <model>.provenance.json with source URL and digest. Both callers (ModelManager downloads and the provisioning tokenizer fetch) pass it. verify_model_integrity now caches a successful check per unchanged file (length, mtime, digest) per process, so multi-GB weights are hashed once, not on every cold load. Hosts that publish no digest remain structurally validated only, stated in README. A test proves a wrong published digest refuses publication, the right one publishes and records provenance, verify_model_integrity passes and then fails after the file is rewritten, and the ETag parser accepts quoted upper-case hex and rejects weak or short tags. cargo test -p susi-gemi-models (255 passed) and -p susi-gemi download (7 passed; download.rs is path-mounted there), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. (This work was first numbered 44 while a parallel Codex session also claimed 44 and EV-2022927-210; that session's governance write overwrote this row, which is re-recorded here as 45.)

RSI iteration 46/100: the leading-MCP control plane (susi mcp enable/disable and zero-config auto-enable) can no longer erase MCP configuration or re-admit servers the user turned off. leading_mcp.rs kept its own reader of mcp_config.json with serde_json::from_str(..).unwrap_or(empty), a duplicate of the GmcpClient reader fixed in iteration 44 with the same fail-open, so a torn config read as empty and enable/disable saved it back with one server, dropping every other configured server. load_user_disabled likewise read a damaged or unreadable user_disabled.json as an empty list: auto_enable_ready then re-enabled every server the user had disabled, and the next disable rewrote the list with a single entry. load_mcp_config now delegates to GmcpClient::read_mcp_config (made pub(crate); one strict reader instead of two), and load_user_disabled returns an error on damage or read failure, which mark/clear and auto_enable_ready propagate instead of acting on an empty list. A test proves the list round-trips, and that on a damaged file load, mark, and clear all fail and leave the file byte-identical. cargo test -p susi-tools leading_mcp (7 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 47/100: a damaged extension-pack state no longer silently resets the operator's pack selection (Mandate 35). ensure_extensions_substrate runs on every zero-config start and read <extensions>/state.json with from_str(..).unwrap_or_default(), treating read errors the same way, so a torn or unreadable state.json became the default state; the function then auto-loaded every discovered pack, including ones the operator had unloaded, and wrote that state back, erasing the chosen active pack and the unload list. load_pack and unload_pack had the same read-then-rewrite shape. read_state now returns an error for damaged or unreadable state (absent is still the default). Zero-config startup, which must not brick, logs the damage and runs on the seeded default pack in memory without rewriting state.json; load_pack and unload_pack refuse with the error; list_packs, which only displays, shows default state. A test damages state.json after seeding and proves startup returns the default pack while leaving the file byte-identical, and an unload refuses and also leaves it untouched. cargo test -p susi-config extension (17 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass (extensions.rs is path-mounted into susi-core).

RSI iteration 48/100: the susi peers CLI no longer reads a damaged roster or ban list as empty. peers_cli.rs kept its own lenient readers of peers.json and peers_banned.json (read_to_string then from_str(..).unwrap_or_default()), duplicating the swarm readers fixed in iterations 37-38 and reopening their failure modes from the operator surface: peers remove rebuilt the ban list from a damaged read and wrote back only the new ban (erasing earlier ones), peers add checked bans against an empty list and rewrote the roster from nothing, and status/list reported a damaged roster as a standalone node. Both readers now delegate to susi_config::cluster_key::read_json_rows_strict (absent is empty, damaged or unreadable is an error). Mutating commands propagate the error; delegate_membership returns 'handled' without local mutation when the roster cannot say who leads; commit_membership skips the push with a note (its target list still re-reads after the local apply); local_cluster_status, which only displays, falls back to empty. Smoke-tested against the real binary with an isolated SUSI_HOME: with a truncated peers.json, susi peers remove and susi peers list now print the parse error and leave the file byte-identical, while the previous build (checked by stashing the change) printed 'no verified peers — this node runs standalone'. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 49/100: an audit of what the daemon actually runs, and a ratchet so unwired features cannot grow. A reachability pass over crates/susi-daemon/src (roots: non-test references from other crates and the root binary, plus lib.rs re-exports; edges: crate::/super::/susi_daemon:: paths and brace imports in non-test code) finds 31 of 119 modules reachable from any production path. The other 88, about 9,441 lines (e.g. world_model, gossip, nat, vfs, hot_reload, marketplace, http_gateway, load_balancer, scheduler, semantic_memory, event_sourcing, root_cause, fault_injection), are compiled and unit-tested only against themselves; git history shows most arrived in the 2026-09-25/26 'swarm-os' vision-bullet phases, and no integration test touches them. README, identity.json, and roadmap.json do not claim them as features, so this is recorded as unwired code, not a false claim. Method cross-checked: brace-form imports from the root binary (use susi_daemon::{..}) were inspected and are re-exports of SusiDaemon/SusiEngineHooks, already rooted through lib.rs; a Python pass and the Rust test agree on 88. The new architecture test unreachable_daemon_modules_only_decrease ports the pass (no new dependencies) and fails if the count exceeds 88; proven by adding an unreferenced module (89, fails) and removing it (88, passes). Whether to wire or delete the 88 is left to the maintainer; the count is recorded in AGENTS.md ratchet items, ARCHITECTURE.md, README, and the SusiDaemon component row. cargo test --test architecture_tests (18 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 50/100: a self-certifying 'compliance framework' is removed (Mandate 1). susi_gawd::compliance defined SusiCompliance with Swarm/RSI/AGI/Autonomous sections whose Default hard-coded every capability to true (AGI cross-domain reasoning, transfer learning, abstract thinking, creativity, common-sense reasoning; RSI self-modification and capability expansion; and so on), then validate() scored those constants and certificate() rendered a compliance certificate. No check inspected the running system, and nothing in the workspace called it (repo-wide search for every exported type found no user outside the file; README, ARCHITECTURE, identity, and roadmap do not cite it). It is deleted (431 lines), and the susi-gawd crate docs now describe the host layer's real compliance surface, the admin compliance audit. Found while extending the iteration-49 reachability pass beyond susi-daemon; that pass's other non-daemon hits (cloud_recovery, live_search, model_cache, pkb) were checked by hand and are real uses the script misses (calls from nested module directories and #[path] mounts), so no further change. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 51/100: the crown's Swarm pillar now checks what its report claims. susi crown verify passed the critical 'swarm' USP whenever gemi.hardware.profile returned a CPU count, while its detail string asserted 'GAWD/GEMI/tools/agents handlers registered', which nothing checked; a composition that failed to wire the GAWD, tools, or agents plane still reported the Swarm pillar as holding. The check now also requires PlaneBus::is_wired for one representative topic per plane (gawd.mission.solve, gemi.hardware.profile, tools.registry.execute, agents.meta.list) and names any unwired plane in the detail. Verified with a live run of the debug binary from an empty directory: swarm holds with 'plane bus gemi.hardware.profile answered (28 cpus); GAWD/GEMI/tools/agents handlers wired' and all_critical_hold is true. cargo test --test crown_verify_tests and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 52/100: the safety veto catches recursive deletion of the root or home in any spelling. SafetyDetector matched the configured destructive_commands as lower-cased literal substrings, so 'rm -rf /' and 'rm -rf ~' were caught but 'rm -fr /', 'rm -r -f /', 'rm --recursive --force ~', 'rm -rf  /' (two spaces), and '/bin/rm -r /*' passed; because exec_command allowlists bash and sh by design (AGENTS.md), any of these could run inside 'sh -c ...'. A token-level check now runs before the pattern list for every audited action: any rm (or a path ending in /rm) with a recursive flag in any short or long spelling whose operands include /, /*, /., ~, ~/, ~/*, /home/ramadoss, /home/ramadoss or their globs is vetoed, after splitting on shell separators and stripping quotes. The allowlist's doc comment, which claimed shells were deliberately absent while bash, sh, python and make are listed, now states the real design: this list is not a sandbox, and shell lines are only as safe as the content checks. Known limitation, stated: content checks remain pattern-based (e.g. an interpreter one-liner deleting via a library call is not parsed). A test blocks seven bypass spellings and does not flag rm -rf target, rm -r ./build, or a non-recursive rm naming ~. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents safety (5 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 53/100: the security veto blocks actions that carry this host's real credentials, not just known vendor prefixes (Mandate 10). SecurityDetector::audit_action only matched the configured secret_tokens prefixes (sk-, ghp_, AIza, xoxb-, github_pat_, and a few others), so an agent goal or exec_command line containing the actual value of HF_TOKEN (hf_..., not in the list), the host bearer SUSI_HOST_TOKEN, or any provider key without a listed prefix passed the governance check untouched. audit_action now first vetoes any argument containing the value of an environment variable named *_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, or *_SECRET (8+ characters), using the same rule the error-metrics and trust-boundary redactors apply; the rule lives once in susi_error::redact as mask_credentials_from (explicit variable list, used by the veto and its test) with mask_env_credentials delegating to it. A test proves a Bearer header carrying a held HF_TOKEN value is vetoed while benign text and a non-credential variable's value (PATH) are not. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents security (4 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 54/100: the Mandate 40 per-client rate limit can no longer be bypassed by rotating IPv6 addresses. RateLimiter keyed buckets by the exact source IpAddr; an IPv6 client is routinely delegated a whole /64 (2^64 addresses), so one host could send each request from a fresh address and never exhaust rate_limit_per_minute, and doing so also filled the 50,000-entry map, whose over-capacity path evicts an arbitrary bucket, resetting other clients' counters. Buckets are now keyed per client: IPv4 as is, IPv4-mapped IPv6 as its IPv4 address (so the same client cannot double its budget across address families), and other IPv6 addresses by their /64 prefix. A test proves two addresses in one /64 share a budget, a neighbouring /64 has its own, and ::ffff:192.0.2.7 shares 192.0.2.7's bucket. cargo test -p susi-core net_guard (10 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 55/100: synthesized Wasm reflexes are published atomically. synthesize_wasm_reflex ran rustc with -o pointing at the live data_dir/reflexes/<slug>.wasm, and ToolRegistry both lists every reflexes/*.wasm as a reflex_<slug> tool and executes it as soon as the file exists, so a concurrent call during compilation could hand WasmHost a half-written module, and a failed recompile could leave a truncated file in place of the previous working reflex. rustc now writes <slug>.wasm.<pid>.tmp (not a .wasm, so never listed or executed), which is renamed over the live name only after a successful build; a spawn failure, a compile failure, or a failed rename removes the staging file and returns the error, leaving any previous reflex intact. Verified with the real toolchain on this host (wasm32-wasip1 installed): a new ignored test synthesizes a probe reflex, checks the \\0asm magic and that no staging file remains, then removes it; run explicitly with --ignored and passing. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 56/100: DAG agents run the command they were given for every shell tag. MissionDag::execute_dag extracts fenced shell blocks from model output and runs them through exec_command, but it stripped the language tag with chained trim_start_matches("bash").trim_start_matches("sh").trim_start_matches("shell"): for a block tagged shell the sh pass removed the first two letters, so the node executed 'ell ...' (a failed or wrong command) instead of the requested one; a tag such as shellscript also matched no rule consistently. shell_block_command now takes the tag as the whole first line of the block and accepts exactly bash, sh, or shell, keeping the existing refusals of empty commands and '!'-prefixed lines. A test covers all three tags, a longer lookalike tag, a non-shell language, a '!' line, and an empty body. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm shell_block and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 57/100: DAG evidence trails bind each task node to its own receipt. After a node's output passed the Truth gate, execute_dag bound its EvidenceRecord to session.receipts().find(|r| r.successful), the first successful receipt of the whole mission session. Every node in the DAG therefore carried the same receipt, usually another node's command or an unrelated earlier tool call, so the Evidence pillar's claim trail misattributed who observed what. Each node run now records the exact receipt arguments of the exec_command calls it issued (the JSON of its wrapped command, which is what capture_call stores), and the node binds the most recent successful exec_command receipt whose arguments match one of its own calls; a node that ran no command binds nothing rather than borrowing another's. Verification is partial and stated as such: the matching relies on receipts recording the call's arguments verbatim (true for capture_call, apart from credential redaction or the 4 KiB argument cap, where the node would then bind nothing), and no end-to-end DAG run with a live model was performed in this iteration. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 58/100: an earlier mission keeps its evidence ledger when a later mission on the same workspace finishes first. EvidenceSession::activate published one active session per canonical workspace, and rayon workers (which never inherit the thread-local current session) record receipts through that slot or through the workspace rendezvous file for vendored copies. A second activation replaced the first, and when the second mission ended its guard removed both the slot and session.json, so the still-running first mission's worker and vendored-copy receipts were silently dropped and its final answer could no longer cite its own tool calls. Activations are now a per-workspace stack: the newest owns the workspace, a finishing activation removes only itself, and if it was the owner the rendezvous file is republished for the mission still running (or removed when none remains). Known limitation, stated: while two missions overlap on one workspace, worker receipts still go to the newer one (attribution by workspace, not by mission); per-mission attribution would need the session carried into worker threads. A regression test activates A then B, ends B, records from a worker thread, and proves the receipt lands in A and not B (the previous code dropped it). cargo test -p susi-core capture (16 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 59/100: the Truth pillar's documentation now matches its deliberately lenient behavior (Mandate 1). Two maintainer commits on 2026-09-26 made missing citations non-fatal: e8ed3223 (verify_mission_with_cross_examine returns the answer with a 'No citations found; answer may be unverified' warning when there is nothing to cite) and 6f5bc4d4 (verify_evidence accepts Unverified records). The code comment still said 'Only a live ledger citation answer can pass here', verify_evidence was still described as the primary verification entrypoint with Ok implying verified, README's pillar read 'absolute sources only', and the identity pillar implied the same. Traced the full path to confirm what actually holds: EvidenceSession::verify_answer still hard-fails uncited narrative whenever the mission captured citable receipts (the error the AMA's auto-citation fallback catches), so the warning path applies only when a mission has nothing to cite; accountability::is_usable does not treat the warning as failure, so such answers complete. The behavior is kept as the maintainer chose; the two doc comments, README pillar 1, and identity pillar 1 now state it precisely. No code behavior changed; cargo fmt --check passes.

RSI iteration 60/100: under local_only, the HTTP inference provider itself refuses to send prompts or embedding text off the host/LAN. local_only enforcement for cloud inference relied on callers: endpoint registration is skipped when the posture is already local_only, and try_providers and a few routing paths drop providers whose names match InferenceRouter::is_cloud_provider_name (vendor substrings or a '-'). A provider registered before an operator switched to local_only in a running daemon, or one named outside that heuristic, reached HttpProvider::generate/embed with no check at all, and embed carries workspace text for the semantic index. The only address-based helper, is_remote_cloud, also counted only https:// non-localhost bases as cloud, so a plain-http internet host did not count as off-host. HttpProvider::generate and embed now call refuse_off_host_under_local_only first: when MacPolicy::blocks_cloud_inference() holds and the endpoint is not on this host or LAN (loopback, RFC1918/unique-local, link-local, localhost/*.localhost/*.local; parsed with url, so localhost.evil.com is remote), the call fails with a [PRIVACY] governance error. Balanced and Open modes, and a local_only host holding a cloud grant, are unchanged. A test classifies six local and five remote bases. cargo test -p susi-gemi (375 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. The gate composes blocks_cloud_inference (covered by the mac_policy tests) with the tested locality rule; a live local_only switch against a remote endpoint was not exercised.

RSI iteration 61/100: model downloads respect the privacy posture. Network egress is gated by MacPolicy::authorize_tool, which only sees MCP/registry tool calls; download::transfer (every model and tokenizer fetch, including the daemon's zero-config auto-prime, susi models installs, and provisioning) and the new published-digest HEAD reached Hugging Face with no check, so a local_only host kept downloading without the egress consent its posture requires. mac_policy now provides egress_permitted(url): host/LAN targets are always allowed; anything else only when the posture does not block network egress by default or an egress grant is held (balanced and open keep working through their default grants). transfer refuses with a [PRIVACY] error that both download retry loops treat as permanent, and published_sha256 skips the lookup. The host/LAN rule moved into mac_policy as a std-only url_stays_local (every crate mounts this module; not all depend on url), and the provider gate from iteration 60 now uses it instead of its own copy (no duplicate). Test only_host_and_lan_urls_stay_local covers six local and six remote forms, including userinfo, bracketed IPv6, localhost.evil.com, and a query string naming localhost. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (11 passed), -p susi-gemi (375 passed), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Observed once and reported, not hidden: download::tests::interrupted_transfer_resumes_and_publishes_atomically failed in one full susi-gemi-models run and passed in 3 targeted and 7 further full runs; it drives a scripted localhost server with 5 s timeouts and is recorded as a suspected timing flake, not resolved here.

RSI iteration 62/100: agent live search no longer sends the mission goal off-host under local_only. SearchAgent calls live_search::gather_live_evidence directly (not through authorize_tool), which fetched Open-Meteo and DuckDuckGo with the goal text and also invoked the brave_search/google_search MCP tools; requirements_for_tool classified those two names as local reads (only web_search/live_search, http, fetch, and similar substrings were egress), so under local_only the goal left the host through every path. fetch_open_meteo_weather and fetch_duckduckgo_instant now require mac_policy::egress_permitted for their API host and fail with a [PRIVACY] governance error otherwise (the attempt is reported in the search result, never faked), and brave_search/google_search are listed in EGRESS_TOOLS so authorize_tool gates them. The one local tool containing 'search', semantic_search, stays a local read; this was checked by listing every tool name containing 'search' in the tree and config before choosing explicit names over a broad substring. A test pins the three web-search tools to network.egress and semantic_search to filesystem.read. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (12 passed), -p susi-gawd-agents live_search (3 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Other direct HTTP clients that bypass authorize_tool (webhook dispatch, HF discovery, external-agent cloud APIs, benchmarks) remain unaudited for posture and are the next items.

RSI iteration 63/100: agent-to-remote calls outside authorize_tool respect the privacy posture. Three swarm paths sent mission data off-host with no MAC check: external peer agents over openai_chat/http/a2a (the POST body is the mission goal, and for http also the workspace path), the native proxy-endpoint agent (POSTs the goal to its configured completion endpoint), and LibraryScoutAgent's crates.io search (a model-derived query term). Each now asks mac_policy::egress_permitted for its target: the external peer dispatch refuses network protocols with a [PRIVACY] governance error (managed/process peers are local processes and unchanged), the proxy agent refuses before building the request, and LibraryScoutAgent skips the live crates.io query and falls through to its existing local-reasoning recommendation. Host/LAN targets and balanced/open postures are unaffected. Audit status stated: webhook_dispatcher was also checked and is not configured by any production path (set_webhook_dispatcher is only called from a test), so it cannot send today; HF discovery, external-agent cloud APIs (susi agents), MCP HTTP clients, and benchmark/eval clients remain unaudited for posture. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents (258 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 64/100: cloud coding agents and Hugging Face catalog discovery respect the privacy posture. susi agents run/send for the Devin and Manus adapters POSTed the user's prompt (and follow-up messages) to api.devin.ai / api.manus.ai with no MAC check, and the model ladder's dynamic discovery queried the Hugging Face API during provisioning; neither goes through authorize_tool. Cloud::new, the single constructor every cloud adapter call uses (execute, refresh, cancel, send), now refuses with a [PRIVACY] error unless mac_policy::egress_permitted allows the adapter's base URL, and fetch_dynamic_ladder returns no dynamic steps under a blocking posture (identical to its existing offline path, so provisioning falls back to the static ladder). Balanced and open postures and granted egress are unchanged. Remaining unaudited direct clients, stated: MCP HTTP transports (susi-core mcp_client, susi-tools client/connection), benchmark/eval, and the A2A server's outbound calls. cargo test -p susi-agents, -p susi-gemi-models hf_discovery, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 65/100: remote MCP/GMCP HTTP calls respect the privacy posture at the transport. mcp_client::post is the single transport for streamable-HTTP MCP calls (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, session teardown) used by remote tool execution, the daemon's zero-config remote scouting, and cluster peer calls. Tool calls routed through MacPolicy::authorize_tool were already gated by name (mcp_* is classified as egress), but scouting and other internal callers reached remote servers with no posture check, sending tool arguments and listings off-host under local_only. post now refuses with a [PRIVACY] error unless mac_policy::egress_permitted(url) holds; host/LAN MCP servers and cluster peers on the LAN keep working, as do balanced/open postures and granted egress. cargo test -p susi-core mcp_client (8 passed), the member_signing, peer_request_signing, endorsements, and cluster_rekey integration tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Egress audit status after iterations 60-65: provider inference/embeddings, model downloads, live search, external peers, the proxy agent, crate scouting, cloud coding agents, HF discovery, and the MCP HTTP transport are gated; benchmark/eval clients (operator-invoked) and susi-tools connection.rs remain unaudited.

RSI iteration 66/100: the leaf-service supervisor detects crash loops instead of counting lifetime crashes. service_table::record increments ServiceRecord.restarts on every respawn and nothing decayed it; it was reset only after the MAX_RESTARTS (10) cap tripped and the 300 s suspension elapsed. A leaf service (susi-native, susi-sandbox, susi-config, ...) that crashed once every few days was therefore suspended on its tenth crash since daemon boot, a five-minute outage of that plane triggered by a pattern that is not a loop. respawn now consults crash_loop_exhausted: if the service ran at least STABLE_RUN_SECS (600 s) since its last start before dying, its budget resets before the cap check, so only crashes close together count toward suspension. A test proves a quick re-death after exhausting the budget still suspends, and a death after a stable run gets a fresh budget. cargo test -p susi-daemon restart_budget and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 67/100: the inspectable mission blackboard uses the one credential redactor and is replaced atomically. persist_inspectable (which writes <workspace>/.susi/last_blackboard.json, the Blackboard pillar's glass-box surface read by susi blackboard and the crown) redacted agent outputs with a private hard-coded list of four prefixes (sk-, ghp_, github_pat_, xoxb-), a duplicate of the governance list that missed its other entries (AIza, AWS key names, private-key headers) and never masked credential values held in the environment. It also wrote the file with an unchecked plain fs::write, so a concurrent reader could parse a torn file. Outputs now go through susi_config::redact_credentials (environment-held *_API_KEY/*_TOKEN/*_SECRET values plus the configured governance.secret_tokens, falling back to the bundled list) and the file is replaced through atomic_write_bytes. The existing test now also stores an AIza key and a ghp_ token and proves neither reaches the file. cargo test -p susi-core agent_types and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 68/100: the other two glass-box mission files are redacted by the shared redactor and replaced atomically. persist_governance_report (fleet.rs, writing .susi/last_governance.json) carried the same private four-prefix redaction list removed from the blackboard in iteration 67, and persist_inspectable_trace (writing .susi/last_mission_trace.json) documented 'no secret bodies' but applied no redaction at all while writing the goal, every A2A interaction payload (which carries tool output), the final answer, and the raw protocol text. Both were plain unchecked fs::write calls, and the crown's glass-box check parses all three files. Governance outcomes now go through susi_config::redact_credentials, the whole trace document is redacted with it before writing, and both files are replaced through atomic_write_bytes. The trace test now puts a ghp_ token in the final answer and proves the written file still parses as JSON and does not contain it. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm (305 passed), -p susi-gawd-agents (258 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. With iteration 67, all three glass-box files the crown reads (last_blackboard, last_governance, last_mission_trace) share one redactor and atomic writes.

RSI iteration 69/100: the Mandate 3 bloat & security audit covers the substrate, not just the CLI. BloatAuditor::audit_workspace (behind susi bloat-audit and gawd.admin.bloat) walked only <workspace>/src: in this repository that is 49 files and 9,950 lines of CLI, while the substrate lives under crates/, so the audit's unwrap/expect/unsafe/secret figures described under a tenth of the code. It also counted unwrap/expect/clone calls inside #[cfg(test)] modules and #[test] functions, which the mandates exempt, and treated an unreadable file as a clean empty scan. The walk now covers every .rs file under the workspace (skipping target/ and dot directories), the AST visitor skips #[cfg(test)] modules and #[test] functions, and a read failure marks the file failed. Measured with a new ignored, read-only test that audits this repository from its source tree: 431 files, 0 parse failures, 111,941 lines, 3,173 production functions, 2 oversized, 65 unwrap, 33 expect, 749 clone, 23 unsafe blocks, 0 TODO markers, 12 secret-pattern line hits (not triaged here; many are pattern definitions and redaction code). A new test proves test-only code is not counted and that crates/ is scanned while target/ is skipped. cargo test -p susi-gawd bloat (9 passed plus the ignored repository audit run explicitly) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Side effect reported: an earlier manual run of the debug CLI during this iteration restarted the operator's running daemon via the binary-integrity check; the repository audit was then measured through the read-only test instead.

RSI iteration 70/100: every panic-path #[allow] now carries a written justification, enforced by a test, and the bloat audit's 'production' figures exclude test-only files. Following up iteration 69's measurement (65 unwrap, 33 expect), a location breakdown showed most hits in integration tests, src/tests/ files mounted under #[cfg(test)] from lib.rs (which carry no attribute of their own), and *_tests.rs files; the audit walk now also skips tests/, benches/, fuzz/, and examples/ directories and *_tests.rs / *_test.rs files. Re-measured with the read-only repository test: 407 files, 107,481 lines, 3,105 functions, 2 oversized, 9 unwrap, 22 expect, 735 clone, 18 unsafe, 0 TODO, 7 secret-pattern line hits; iteration 69's README row overstated production unwrap/expect and is corrected. AGENTS.md makes an #[allow] without a written justification a compliance violation: a scan of all 20 panic-path allows found 5 justified inside the function body and 2 with none (susi-agents registry::bootstrap_data and susi-config SusiConfig::bundled_defaults, both include_str! bundled-default parses), which now carry Mandate 42 comments; bus.rs subscribe gained a pointer to its justification nine lines down. New architecture test every_panic_path_allow_is_justified fails on any allow of unwrap_used/expect_used/panic/unreachable/todo/unimplemented/wildcard_enum_match_arm in non-test sources without a // comment on the line, directly above, or within the next 8 lines; it failed on bus.rs before the pointer was added. cargo test --test architecture_tests (19 passed), -p susi-gawd bloat, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 71/100: secret detection no longer fires inside ordinary words. Triaging the bloat audit's secret-pattern hits in production sources showed all seven were false positives, mostly the bundled sk- prefix inside words (ta-sk-queue, di-sk-backed, ri-sk-). The same raw substring matching drove two live paths: SecurityDetector::audit_action vetoed any goal containing such a word as a leaked key (e.g. 'write a risk-assessment doc'), and the shared redactor rewrote 'task-queue' as 'ta[REDACTED]' across error metrics and, since iterations 67-68, the blackboard, governance, and mission-trace files. One rule now lives in susi_error::redact: secret_match_starts yields only occurrences where the preceding character is not ASCII alphanumeric; redact_patterns (via redact_one), the new contains_secret_pattern (used by the SecurityDetector veto), and the bloat auditor all use it. Tokens after spaces, '=', ':', or punctuation still match, so the existing property tests (any tail after a prefix is redacted) and the error-metrics redaction test pass unchanged. New tests: ordinary words are neither redacted nor flagged while key=sk-... and (AIza...) are; the security veto accepts 'write a risk-assessment doc'. Re-measured audit: secret-pattern hits 7 -> 4 (remaining are comments naming prefixes and the crown's deliberate ghp_ probe). cargo test -p susi-error (11), -p susi-gawd-agents (259), -p susi-config (44), -p susi-core (208), -p susi-gawd-swarm (306), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 72/100: the safety veto's critical-path check matches whole absolute path components instead of substrings. SafetyDetector checked governance.critical_system_paths (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /boot, /proc, /sys, /dev) with lower-cased contains(), so for write_file, exec_command, and every SUSI_SOLVE goal it vetoed ordinary work: 'cargo build in ~/dev/myapp' (a common home layout) was refused as targeting '/dev', as were ./dev/notes.md, docs/bootstrap.md ('/boot'), /systemd-units ('/sys'), and /processing ('/proc'). Confirmed with a failing test before the change. names_absolute_path now requires the match to start at a boundary (not after a letter, digit, ~, ., /, _ or -, so it is not inside another path) and to end the component (end of text or a character other than a letter, digit, _, - or .). Stated trade-off: a sibling like /etc/passwd- (a shadow backup name) is no longer caught by the /etc/passwd entry; operators can list it explicitly. A test allows five legitimate goals and blocks five that really name /etc/shadow, /dev/sda, /boot, /proc/sys/..., and '/sys/firmware'. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents safety (6 passed), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 73/100: destructive-command and exfiltration patterns match whole commands, not text inside other words. Both detectors matched their configured lists with lower-cased contains(): the exfiltration entry 'nc -e' fired inside 'rsync -e ssh', so a routine deploy step was vetoed as network exfiltration, and the destructive entry 'dd if=' fired inside 'add if= guard'. Both failures were confirmed with tests before the change. Both loops now use susi_error::redact::secret_match_starts (the token-start rule introduced in iteration 71, documented as shared), so a pattern counts only where it begins a token. Real invocations still veto: 'nc -e /bin/sh ...' and 'dd if=/dev/zero of=disk.img' are blocked, and the crown's governance probe (rm -rf / and the env-wrapper bypass) still holds. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents (262 passed), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. With iterations 71-72, every configured governance pattern list (secret tokens, critical paths, destructive commands, exfiltration vectors) is now boundary-aware.

RSI iteration 74/100: the natural-intent classifier reads its config-driven keyword lists and matches whole words. config.default.json ships intent_classify (query_exact, query_prefixes, query_contains, motion_contains) and SusiConfig::intent_classify() exposes it as 'no hardcoded keyword lists in Rust' (Mandate 35), but nothing read it: classify_natural_intent hard-coded the same lists, so operator edits had no effect. It also used substring checks, so goals mentioning 'promotion' or 'emotion' were typed [MOTION] Architectural Evolution when ingested into the evidence memory; the reflex fallback branch repeated the substring checks on the reflex reply (confirmed in testing: with a live daemon answering pulse_reason, 'draft a promotion plan' still came back [MOTION] until that branch was fixed too). The classifier now loads intent_classify from config for the query and motion rules, and every keyword test in both branches (config lists and the reflex reply's query/status/identity/motion/recompile/mission/solve) goes through contains_phrase, a whole-word matcher. Tests: whole-word matching (architecture and 'who am i' match; promotion and emotions do not) and config-driven classification (architecture -> MOTION, status -> QUERY, promotion not MOTION). Note: the classification test runs against whatever plane bus is reachable, which on this host included the live daemon. cargo test -p susi-gawd intent_classify (2 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 75/100: the bundled configuration no longer advertises settings that do nothing. Following iteration 74 (an unread intent_classify section), every SusiConfig accessor was checked for callers (all used) and every top-level key of config/config.default.json was searched for as a quoted string or identifier across crates/ and src/. Four keys are read by nothing and have no hard-coded twin: susi_repo, stdin_timeout_secs (no stdin timeout exists), beacon_interval_secs (no beacon feature exists), and susi_alpha_default (reflex weights are addressed through alpha_weights_filename/alpha_weights_url). An operator editing them saw no effect, and two implied behavior SUSI does not have. They are removed from the bundled defaults (existing host configs keep them harmlessly; merge only adds missing keys). external_peer_agents_note, also unread, is documentation for operators and is kept. cargo test -p susi-config (44 passed), -p susi-sandbox (29 passed), --test architecture_tests (19 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 76/100: the Sovereign Dashboard reports the activity SUSI actually audits instead of invented categories (Mandate 2). susi sovereign-dashboard and the sovereign_dashboard MCP tool counted audit-log lines containing SELF_HEALING, SECURITY_HARDENING or MASKED, OPTIMIZATION or BLOAT_REJECTION, and MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION, and printed them as 'Autonomous Self-Heals', 'Security Hardening Pulses', 'Bloat Rejection Optimizations', and 'Neural Memory Distillations'. A repo-wide search found no code that ever logs any of those event types (the logged types include LATENCY_VIOLATION, INFERENCE_PLACEMENT, SUBSTRATE_AUDIT, EVOLUTION_DRIFT_AUDIT, HALLUCINATION_DETECTED, RELEASE_CUT, and the *MISSION_START family), so the dashboard displayed zeros for work that is never recorded, or a false count whenever an unrelated entry's text merely mentioned one of the words. It now parses each entry and counts it by its real type field, sorted by frequency, and says so plainly when there is no audited activity; the recent-activity trace is unchanged. A test writes three entries (one mentioning SELF_HEALING in its details) and proves the counts are LATENCY_VIOLATION 2 and MISSION_START 1 with no 'Self-Heals' category. cargo test -p susi-gmcp sovereign_dashboard and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 77/100: the autonomous drift audit's bottleneck section reports real failure events. EvolutionManager::detect_bottlenecks (part of perform_autonomous_drift_audit) counted 'Mission Failures' as entries of type MISSION_FAILED or TOOL_FAILURE, which no code logs, plus any entry whose details merely contained 'failed' (so 'retry the failed build' in a MISSION_START counted as a failure), then appended canned 'Recommended Genome Mutations' (a GPU-accelerated reflex, specialist agent synthesis) that nothing acts on and that were unrelated to the data. It now reports reflex latency violations and, per event type, the failure-signal events the substrate actually logs (types ending _FAILED, _VIOLATION, or _DETECTED, e.g. MOTION_RULE_PUSH_FAILED, HALLUCINATION_DETECTED, READINESS_VIOLATION), and drops the canned advice. A test writes a latency violation, a HALLUCINATION_DETECTED, and a MISSION_START mentioning 'failed', and proves the first two are counted, the third is not, and no mutation advice appears. cargo test -p susi-gawd evolution (2 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

anchor.label: unmeasured status claims (reflex_trainer, host_hooks, LibraryScoutAgent, mission_cli, master banner)

entries.milestone: RSI iteration 78/100: five outputs that asserted states nothing measured now say what is known (Mandates 1-2). A search for 'optimal', '100%', 'fully operational' and similar in user-facing strings found: ReflexTrainer::audit_distillation_state reporting 'Reflex substrate optimal.' whenever fewer staged samples than the threshold existed (now 'No reflex training due: fewer than N valid staged samples'); the swarm's unwired NoOpHostHooks returning Ok('Reflex substrate optimal (host hooks unwired)') although nothing was audited (now a [HOST_UNWIRED] internal error; its only caller, the AMAS loop, discards the result); LibraryScoutAgent answering 'Substrate libraries optimal.' to status/ls-style goals it does not analyze (now 'No library scouting applies to this query.'); the model-download report printing 'SUCCESS: 32b and 72b model download agent verified and fully operational' whatever models the steps actually covered (now 'all N download steps completed and verified', printed only when every step is COMPLETED as before); and the master trace banner claiming '100% Omni-Trace Coverage Active', a figure nothing computes (now 'Omni-Trace active'). No test asserted the old strings. Also recorded for iteration 77: README now notes the drift audit's bottleneck section. cargo test -p susi-gawd reflex (12 passed), -p susi-gawd-swarm (309), -p susi-gawd-agents (262), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 79/100: one OS-clean implementation instead of two. susi os-clean ran HardwareProfiler::execute_os_clean, which removed only an oversized rotated error-metrics file, while susi os clean ran os_cli::clean, which removes that same file plus a stale pre-rotation audit.log and oversized stray binaries in ~/.susi/bin; the two commands promised the same thing ('remove SUSI-owned residue') and did different amounts of it. os-clean now calls os_cli::clean (made pub(crate)) and execute_os_clean is deleted. The 64 MiB metrics rotation cap had been copied into hardware.rs twice beside the shared susi-error sink constant from iteration 40; the vendored error module now exposes sink publicly and the remaining audit uses crate::susi_error::sink::METRICS_CAP_BYTES, leaving one definition. The OS-care report's status for 'nothing to reclaim' is renamed from OPTIMAL to NOTHING_RECLAIMABLE (no consumer matched the old string). cargo test -p susi-gemi-models (259 passed), cargo test --bin susi, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 80/100: audit and admin commands run deterministic checks and real tools instead of asking the model swarm to narrate them. susi audit ('Perform compliance audit and technical verification') sent the audit_pulse to ama.solve_clean, while susi admin audit already ran the static SusiAdmin::audit_compliance (its own comment: 'Use fast static compliance audit instead of LLM agent swarm'); two commands promised the same audit and one produced model narration, the failure mode the sovereign-dashboard code records as fabricated '100%' health figures. susi admin verify ('Verify version alignment') likewise asked the swarm although SusiAdmin::verify_version_alignment exists, and susi admin lint ('Run clippy') and audit-deps ('Run cargo audit') asked the swarm to run tools and report on them. Now: susi audit calls audit_compliance (same as admin audit); admin verify calls verify_version_alignment and exits non-zero on mismatch; admin lint runs cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and admin audit-deps runs cargo audit, with inherited output and the tool's exit status. The now-unread admin pulses (audit_pulse, verify_pulse, lint_pulse, audit_deps_pulse, plus uninstall_pulse, which nothing ever read) are removed from AdminPulses and config.default.json (unknown host keys stay preserved by the struct's flattened registry). cargo test -p susi-config (44), --bin susi, --test architecture_tests (19), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 81/100: susi bloat-audit and susi deep-scan run their real implementations. The bloat-audit command sent the literal goal 'bloat_audit' to the swarm (ama.solve_clean), so the operator got a mission narration (observed in iteration 69 as a model trace instead of the auditor's report) rather than BloatAuditor's measured counts; deep-scan likewise sent deep_scan_pulse to the swarm although ModelManager::deep_scan_home_and_register performs the scan and registration deterministically (and is what the GEMI plane's gemi.models.scan topic already calls). bloat-audit now calls BloatAuditor::audit_workspace and render_report for the working directory, and deep-scan calls deep_scan_home_and_register for the substrate config dir; both exit non-zero on error. The now-unread deep_scan_pulse is removed from AdminPulses and config.default.json. Remaining swarm-driven CLI pulses, stated: install (provisioning narration), select-model, and mcp-scout. cargo test -p susi-config (44), --bin susi, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 82/100: susi select-model writes the model override itself, and the override rejects names that would corrupt it. The command substituted the model name into select_model_pulse and sent it to the swarm (ama.solve_clean), so whether the override was actually written depended on a model choosing to do it, while ModelManager::set_selected_model (already used by the gemi.models.select topic) writes it deterministically. It now calls set_selected_model directly and exits non-zero on failure. set_selected_model accepted any string: an empty name wrote an empty selected_model_override.txt, which every inference reads as 'no override', while reporting the override 'set to '''; a newline or other control character would split the one-line file. It now rejects empty, over-512-character, and control-character names before writing. The unread select_model_pulse is removed from AdminPulses and config.default.json. A test proves empty, whitespace, newline, tab, and oversized names are rejected (they return before any write, so the test never touches the real config dir). cargo test -p susi-gemi-models selection_tests, -p susi-config (44), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Remaining swarm-driven pulses: install and mcp-scout.

RSI iteration 83/100: the host configuration can no longer be seeded from the current directory. When ~/.susi/config.json did not exist, ensure_global_sandbox_locally (behind SandboxManager::ensure_global_sandbox, used by first-run provisioning) read Path::new("config.default.json"), a path relative to the process's working directory, and installed it as the host's global config if it parsed. Running SUSI for the first time inside any repository that ships a file with that name (including a hostile clone) adopted that repository's governance patterns (secret tokens, destructive commands, critical paths), inference endpoints and API bases, and privacy settings as the host configuration. The seed is now always SusiConfig::default(), which is the bundled config.default.json compiled into the binary via include_str!. A repo-wide search for other working-directory-relative reads of .json/.toml/.env/.key files (Path::new, PathBuf::from, read_to_string with a bare file name) found none. cargo test -p susi-sandbox and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass; the change removes a branch and was not exercised with a crafted working directory (changing a test process's cwd would race parallel tests).

RSI iteration 84/100: susi install initializes the substrate itself. Its first step sent install_pulse ('initialize sandboxed .susi environment and provision weights') to the model swarm and printed the narration, so whether the substrate home and config were created depended on a model acting and the output could claim provisioning that did not happen. The command now calls SandboxManager::ensure_global_sandbox (the deterministic initializer, which after iteration 83 seeds only from the bundled defaults), prints the real outcome, and exits non-zero on failure; its existing background-priming notice and identity handshake are unchanged. The unread install_pulse is removed from AdminPulses and config.default.json, leaving mcp_scout_pulse as the only admin pulse (web scouting is inherently model-driven). cargo test -p susi-config (44), --bin susi, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Iterations 80-84 together moved audit, verify, lint, audit-deps, bloat-audit, deep-scan, select-model, and install off model narration onto their real implementations.

RSI iteration 85/100: the model-provisioning verifier is named and described for what it does. ModelManager::verify_and_provision_32b_and_72b_models, the susi verify-download-agent help ('...and 32b/72b model provisioning'), and the verify_model_download_agent MCP tool description ('ensure 32b and 72b models are provisioned') all promised 32B and 72B models, but the function walks HardwareProfiler::get_progressive_model_ladder, the hardware-selected ladder (whatever sizes fit the host), and reports each step's download state; iteration 78 already removed the matching '32b and 72b ... fully operational' success line. The function is renamed verify_and_provision_model_ladder (both callers updated) and both descriptions now say 'the hardware-selected model ladder'. No behavior change. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 86/100: self-validation checks what it claims, and its failures are errors. execute_autonomous_self_validation reported '- Genome Integrity: N Compiled Rules Verified.' after only counting AlphaSelf::RULES, and logged 'Autonomous foundational readiness test completed.' although no test ran; the self_validate MCP tool ('Execute autonomous substrate self-validation') also returned Ok('# Substrate Self-Validation Failed ...') on error, which EvidenceSession records as a successful, citable receipt. The report now performs one real check, that the compiled genome is non-empty and every rule has a non-blank title and imperative, and fails with a governance error otherwise; the line reads 'Compiled Genome: N rules, each with a title and an imperative'; the audit event says a report was generated. The MCP tool returns Err on failure, and its description now says what it does (report the hardware profile and tensor device, and check the compiled genome). cargo test -p susi-gmcp (247), -p susi-gawd (374), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 87/100: two read-modify-write paths no longer proceed unlocked when their cross-process lock is unavailable. FileLock::acquire returns None after about 3 s of contention or a wedged holder; most call sites bail on None (commit log, service table, audit chain, reflex staging), but two bound it as let _lock = ... and continued: ContextGraph::persist, which rewrites the whole graph log (an unlocked rewrite can replace the file under a sibling's append, silently dropping it), and peer_registry::persist_verified_peer_to, whose own comment said 'Skipping on lock failure converges anyway' while the code performed the roster read-modify-write without the lock. persist now returns a filesystem error and skips compaction (its callers already treat compaction as best effort), and persist_verified_peer_to returns without writing, as its comment described (the peer re-verifies on its next signed handshake). Audit method: every FileLock::acquire site was listed; commit_log::check_term_at, which continues but saves only when the lock is held, is correct and unchanged. cargo test -p susi-core context_graph (9), -p susi-gawd-swarm peer_registry (4), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 88/100: reading recent audit activity no longer loads the whole audit chain. read_audit_log (used by the drift audit's frequent-intent and bottleneck analysis and by the sovereign dashboard) read .susi/audit.log in full with read_to_string on every call, split it into lines, and kept the last N. The workspace audit log is an append-only HMAC chain that is never rotated, so the cost grew with the workspace's whole history, and one invalid UTF-8 byte anywhere made the call return an empty string, which callers render as 'no activity'.
