A new tail_lines reads backwards from the end in 64 KiB chunks only until it holds more than N newlines, and decodes lossily. entries.milestone: Security fix for the SUSI Builder OS workflow. (1) Script injection: the `Execute SUSI Mission` step interpolated `${{ github.event.issue.title }}` and `${{ inputs.goal }}` directly into its bash `run:` block, so an issue title such as `"; curl ... $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` would execute with OPENAI/ANTHROPIC/GROQ secrets and a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN in env. Event data (event_name, goal, issue number/title, PR number) is now passed through step `env:` (EVENT_NAME, GOAL, ISSUE_NUMBER, ISSUE_TITLE, PR_NUMBER) and referenced as quoted shell variables; the commit step's issue-number uses and `$BRANCH_NAME` are likewise env-sourced and quoted. The only remaining `${{ }}` inside `run:` blocks are `github.workspace` and `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which are not attacker-controlled. (2) Trigger authorization: `startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/susi build')` let any commenter start the job, and the unscoped label check also let any comment on a `susi-build`-labeled issue start it. The job `if:` now scopes each clause to its event (`issues`, `pull_request`, `issue_comment`) and requires `github.event.comment.author_association` in OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR for every comment trigger. Label triggers stay ungated because applying a label already requires triage access. workflow_dispatch and trusted-user behavior are unchanged. Verification: the workflow parses with PyYAML; `bash -n` passes on every `run:` block; the extracted mission script, run against a stub `susi` with ISSUE_TITLE containing `"; touch PWNED; echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, backticks, and `$(...)`, and with GOAL containing `$(touch PWNED4); "; id`, passed both strings literally as the solve argument and created no files. actionlint was NOT run because it is not installed and neither Go nor Docker is available on this host. Residual risk, not addressed here: the issue title still reaches the agent as prompt text, so prompt injection into `susi solve` (which has gh/exec tools and a write token) is a separate concern.

Release-only local susi. Two dev paths used to overwrite ~/.susi/bin/susi, the binary the daemon always runs: the xtask post-build install (`cargo xb` / build-gpu.sh), and `auto_install::push_to_hardware_if_dev_build`, which copied any target/ binary over the install on every CLI run. Both are removed. `cargo xb` now only builds, and the auto_install module, its two call sites, and `build_identity` are deleted. The one path in is `scripts/susi-release-sync.sh`. It resolves the newest vX.Y.Z tag and builds it in a private checkout and target dir, targeting this GPU's compute capability; the CI CUDA asset is sm_75 and lacks candle's sm_80+ bf16 kernels. It checks `--version` against the tag, waits until no susi client process is running, and swaps atomically, keeping susi.prev. It then restarts susi.service or the daemon and rolls back if GEMI /health does not answer within 60s. An hourly systemd user timer runs it (`--install-timer`), and `susi release` starts it non-blocking after pushing a new tag. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --locked; the script's --check, busy-client detection, daemon detection, and /health probe were exercised against the live host.

Dev binaries run their own instance. Before this, a target/ binary with default env talked to the release daemon: ensure_daemon_running prefers ~/.susi/bin/susi when it exists, and both shared ~/.susi and ports 9090–9094, so daemon-side dev changes never ran. Now `dev_instance::isolate_if_dev_build` runs first in main, while the process is single-threaded. Any binary other than the installed one (a `(deleted)` swapped-out release daemon still counts as installed) sets SUSI_HOME=~/.susi-dev and SUSI_PORT_OFFSET=100 unless they are already set. It symlinks the release instance's models/ and cloud.env into the dev root; config, audit chain, locks, and ports stay separate. The existing SUSI_HOME machinery does the rest: no ~/.susi-dev/bin/susi means the daemon re-execs the dev binary, the systemd transient unit name is hashed from the instance home, and systemd-run forwards SUSI_*. release-sync's --version probe pins SUSI_HOME so it never provisions ~/.susi-dev. Verified live: `target/debug/susi start` brought up a daemon whose /proc exe is target/debug/susi with SUSI_HOME=~/.susi-dev and SUSI_PORT_OFFSET=100. It served /health 200 on 9191, nothing listened on 9091, and ~/.susi/bin/susi mtime and size were unchanged. Also verified: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --locked.

Mandate 48 "Self-Build Order (Release-Only Toolchain, Isolated Dev Instances)" added to identity DNA. It binds SUSI's swarm, A2A delegates, and human developers to three rules: build dev in target/ only, verify dev on the ~/.susi-dev instance (9190–9194), and change ~/.susi/bin/susi only through a tagged release promoted by scripts/susi-release-sync.sh (installer excepted, Mandate 47). Engine protocol 7 (Canonical Binary Dynamics) now names those two writers. Design principle 9 was added, and README and AGENTS.md cite the mandate. Because identity.json compiles into the agent genome (susi-gawd-agents build.rs, GEN_AGENT_RULES), the rule reaches SUSI's own agents, not only docs. Mechanical guard: tests/architecture_tests.rs dev_builds_never_install_the_release_binary rejects fs::copy/fs::rename/".susi" in xtask, any non-test push_to_hardware/auto_install, dev_instance isolation after Cli::parse, and a missing sync script. It is scoped under Mandate 1 as a targeted guard, not a proof, and makes no claim that releases can't break. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --locked (genome rebuild included).

"SUSI writes SUSI" audit and fixes for Mandate 48. Before this: the constitution compiled into the genome reached only reports (identity_report, the substrate report, a filtered stderr trace), not the prompts of SUSI's code-writing agents. prompts.json system_identity is one line, and dynamic_agent_prompt carries only role, goal, and blackboard. Delegated external agents got the bare task; Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor read AGENTS.md themselves, aider and Gemini CLI do not. apply_patch_cycle verified self-patches with `cargo test` only. susi-builder.yml built its builder from the branch under change and pushed directly to main on manual and PR triggers; on PR events it would push from a detached merge ref. Fixes: `susi_core::self_build` detects a SUSI tree (root Cargo.toml `name = "susi"` plus .agents/identity.json) and prepends BRIEF, the Mandate 48 contract. BRIEF covers: build into target/ only, verify on the dev instance, pass the fmt/clippy/test gate, and commit on a branch without pushing to main, tagging, or releasing. It is prepended to every Execution-catalog coding agent's task (browser-use/openviking/deerflow excluded as non-coding) after the caller's prompt is audited, and to MissionDag shell-node prompts. patch_cycle defaults to VERIFY_COMMAND in a SUSI tree. susi-builder.yml installs the released susi via install.sh as the builder, runs the verify gate, and lands work as a PR on susi-mission/*, or on a same-repo PR's head branch; it opens a draft PR when the gate fails. Guarded by tests/architecture_tests.rs self_build_contract_reaches_every_code_writing_path and susi-core self_build unit tests. Scope (Mandate 1): this states and checks the contract at every known code-writing entry. It does not prove an LLM obeys it; the release gate and PR review remain the enforcement. Verification: cargo fmt --all --check and clippy -D warnings pass. The full cargo test --workspace run passes except susi-gawd-a2a execute_without_message_reports_failed_task and execute_with_non_text_part_reports_failed_task. Those two also fail on the tree without this change; they are host-state dependent and fail while the release daemon is running.

Compiled genome rules now carry their real source and citation instead of synthetic numbers. build.rs used to give DNA mandates their own IDs, roadmap vectors 50+seq, engine protocols 100+id, and ledger entries 150+seq. Ledger IDs use seven counters (EV-2022920 through EV-2022928), so the offsets collided: EV-2022920-031 and EV-2022924-031 were both 181. Every consumer also printed them as mandates. The mission trace's [GENOMIC MANDATES] block filtered on titles containing Universal/Agnosticism; no current mandate matches, so it showed a ledger entry as "Mandate 352" (seen in the v0.15.2 release smoke). SusiAxiomRule now has `kind: RuleKind` (Mandate / EngineProtocol / RoadmapVector / Evidence) and `cite`, which follows identity.json canonical_addressing: `Mandate N`, `Pillar IV item N`, or the vector or ledger ID. The trace lists only mandates under that heading, with a per-kind summary. Identity reports, the substrate report, the tri-state line, and genome distillation cite rules by source, and the single "Hardcoded Axiom Rules: 338" total is replaced by counts per kind. Ledger entries with no numeric suffix are no longer silently dropped. Test every_rule_is_cited_by_its_real_source asserts unique citations and correct prefixes per kind. Verified live on the dev instance: `target/debug/susi identity` printed "[GENOMIC MANDATES] 48 mandates, 7 engine protocols, 2 roadmap vectors, 281 ledger entries", then Mandate 1 through 48. Checks: cargo fmt and clippy -D warnings clean. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast: 1048 passed, 2 failed; the failures are the known host-dependent susi-gawd-a2a tests, which fail while the release daemon runs.

entries.milestone: RSI iteration 1-3 (Claude run): leaf-service HTTP shells extracted into `susi-leaf-services`; foundation crates lose axum/tokio.
entries.proof: Before: `susi-paths`, `susi-error`, `susi-config`, `susi-sandbox` and `susi-native` each embedded an axum server (`serve`), a tokio runtime bootstrap, and a `main.rs`; four separate `require_bearer` middlewares existed with two policies (`susi-error` and `susi-native` carried byte-identical private `leaf_authorized` copies). After: one crate, `crates/susi-leaf-services`, holds the runtime/bind helper, the two bearer policies as middleware (`host_token` over `susi_paths::bearer_authorized`, `supervisor` over the moved `susi_paths::supervisor_bearer_authorized`), five routers and the `service-run` dispatch (`src/cli/control_plane_cli.rs` now calls `susi_leaf_services::serve`); the five binaries keep their names so `LEAF_SERVICES` spawning is unchanged. Dependencies removed: axum+tokio from susi-paths, susi-error, susi-config; axum+serde+serde_json+susi-paths from susi-sandbox (tokio narrowed to `time`); axum+tokio+serde+serde_json+susi-paths from susi-native; serde from susi-paths. Bugs fixed on the way: (1) `susi-error`'s event client posted to `SUSI_ERROR_PORT` or a hard-coded 18081, ignoring the instance offset, so a dev instance (`~/.susi-dev`, offset 100) reported its errors to the release instance's service — now `susi_error::service_port()` = `ports::effective(18081)`; (2) the standalone `susi-paths`/`susi-config` binaries shifted their port by the env offset only while `LeafService::port()` also honours the config-file `port_offset` — every binary now resolves through `LeafService::port()`. Also cleared three pre-existing `-D warnings` clippy failures on main (`byte_char_slices` in susi-paths, `too_many_arguments` on `susi_http_transport::client::http_call_with_body` — justified allow, not a signature change, because another agent is actively editing its ten callers — and `redundant_closure` in susi-gemi `http_provider.rs`). (3) CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) polled `susi-native`'s `/healthz` but no leaf service ever routed it (only the plain-port fallback could succeed): every leaf service now answers an unauthenticated `GET /healthz` from the shared `run` helper, and the CI step builds the binary from its new crate (`cargo build -p susi-leaf-services --bin susi-native`). Verified: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean. Tests not run per operator instruction (separate chore after the 100 iterations); `tests/architecture_tests.rs` LEAF_RANK gained `susi-leaf-services` at rank 5 so the leaf-order test stays consistent.

entries.proof: A per-crate scan (declared dependency name absent from that crate's src/tests/benches/build.rs and not referenced by a feature) found 63 dead declarations across 16 manifests: `crossbeam` in 10 of the 11 crates declaring it (only `susi-core/src/queue.rs` used it), `regex`/`dashmap`/`parking_lot`/`flume`/`tracing`/`tokio`/`rayon`/`shlex`/`serde` in the feature planes, `susi-paths` in susi-gawd-a2a and susi-server, unused `proptest` dev-dependencies in 11 crates, and the root package's Windows-only `winapi` (no `winapi` reference anywhere in the root sources). All removed; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` compiling afterwards is the proof none was a false positive on Linux. Then: (1) `susi-paths` replaces `directories` with a std-only `xdg` module reproducing `ProjectDirs::from("", "intellibitz", "susi")` exactly per OS (Linux `$XDG_*`/`~/.config|.local/share|.cache` + `susi`, relative XDG values ignored; macOS `~/Library/{Application Support,Caches}/intellibitz.susi`; Windows `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%\\intellibitz\\susi\\{config,data,cache}`) — only divergence: no `getpwuid` fallback when `$HOME` is unset (needs `unsafe`, forbidden in this crate), same `USERPROFILE`/`.` fallback the crate already used; `susi-paths` now depends only on `serde_json`. (2) `once_cell::sync::Lazy` → `std::sync::LazyLock` (3 sites; workspace dep deleted). (3) `md5` removed from susi-gawd-swarm: the AMA master hashed a TRUTH_VIOLATION error string only to put it in an in-memory `HashSet` for retry-loop detection — the text is now the key. (4) `susi-core`'s pulse queue swaps crossbeam `SegQueue` for two unbounded `flume` lanes holding both channel ends (non-blocking `try_recv` pop, cannot disconnect). Verified: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Tests not run per operator instruction.

entries.milestone: External agent runs can no longer rewrite the workspace's git identity. Incident: 99 commits from 2026-09-27 were authored as "Your Name <you@example.com>" because the repo-local .git/config gained placeholder user.name/user.email. Root cause (read from aider 0.86.2 aider/main.py setup_git): aider runs `git config --get user.name/user.email` and writes those placeholders into the repo-local config when either is missing. The launch path was tests/empirical_validation_tests.rs test_empirical_epistemic_integrity_fictitious. It isolated HOME to a temp dir but used the checkout as the workspace, and before 8c66b337 cloud_recovery::recover fell through to its ultimate external-agent fallback. That fallback launched aider in the real repo 12 times (.susi/execution-agents/a30910b6…, prompt "inspect the status of cargo module non_existent_quantum_crank", 2026-09-27 21:38 onward). Fix: process::execute arms GitIdentityGuard for every local process adapter. Its probes use the agent's exact env. In a git work tree with no visible identity it refuses to launch. Otherwise it pins GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* to the visible identity, and after the run (success, failure or cancel) it restores any repo-local user.name/user.email the agent changed, flagging the run's error field. GIT_AUTHOR_* alone was rejected because `git config --get` ignores it. aider --no-git (the only flag that skips setup_git) was rejected as the default because it also disables aider's repo map and commits; --no-auto-commits and --git-commit-verify do not prevent the write. The empirical test now runs missions in a scratch workspace and asserts no execution-agents run was created. Regression tests: git_identity::tests (isolated-HOME refusal writes nothing; aider-style placeholder write restored plus author env pinned; non-repo unguarded) and external::tests::agent_run_cannot_rewrite_workspace_git_identity (end-to-end through AgentManager). Dev-instance check (target/debug/susi, isolated HOME → .susi-dev, ~/.susi/bin untouched) with real aider 0.86.2 in scratch repos: raw aider as a control wrote the placeholders; susi refused the same launch and left .git/config clean; with identity present aider ran (exit 0) and identity was unchanged. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast (1048 passed, 0 failed; a first fail-fast run hit 2 susi-gawd-a2a failures that passed in isolation and on rerun, and that crate does not depend on susi-agents). Scope: guards repo-local user.name/user.email only; aider still adds .aider* to .gitignore unless --no-gitignore.

Known-failure patterns now lower plan rank rather than merely forcing consensus. Coverage baseline stray keys folded into floor_percent; floors moved to honest measurements (susi-config 74, susi-tools 59, susi-gawd 58.5, susi-core 87, susi-gawd-swarm 52).
entries.proof: New tests: failing_tools_flags_only_unambiguous_failures (susi-core 205 pass), failed_history_tools_penalize_but_do_not_veto (susi-gawd-swarm 54 pass). susi-tools +7 plane-handler/types tests (19 pass; plane_handler.rs 40->90% lines).

entries.milestone: Tier-0 reflex checkpoints are no longer published blindly. Before: SusiAlphaModel::train_on_staged_file trained 100 epochs on every claimed batch and always published the result, so one bad or contradictory batch silently replaced a working reflex model. Now holdout_gate holds out one in five staged intents (SHA-256 of the normalized intent mod 5, stable across cycles). It fits a candidate from the active weights on the rest and requires held-out accuracy >= the active checkpoint's; the active model scores only within its own vocabulary. A regression returns an error, so ReflexTrainer restores the claim, and the active checkpoint is kept. On pass, the checkpoint is refit on all samples and published. Skipped, with the reason in the report, when there is no active checkpoint or fewer than 3 held-out samples. Training was refactored into ReflexNet (init/fit/correct) with one batched projection. Tests: holdout_split_is_stable_and_about_one_in_five; prediction_scoring_counts_only_the_expressible_vocabulary; regressing_checkpoint_is_held_back_and_improving_one_publishes (cycle 1 publishes with no active checkpoint; cycle 2's contradicting train split is held back with the checkpoint unchanged; cycle 3's consistent data passes and publishes). That test passed 10 of 10 repeated runs from random init. Scope: the gate measures held-out intent-classification accuracy only, not downstream reflex outcomes.

Failed missions no longer train the Tier-0 reflex classifier. Before: SusiMissionReport::emit_mission_trace staged goal -> action for every mission. The outcome (FAILED/BLOCKED/...) was recorded only in performance_metadata, and parse_training_entries ignored it. Because the classifier has no negative class, each failed mission taught the model to map that goal to the action that had just failed. Now there are two independent guards. The source (ama/report.rs) stages only when MissionTrace::succeeded() (SUCCESS/COMPLETE). The trainer (alpha.rs parse_training_entries) skips any record whose performance_metadata.outcome is present and not a success, which covers samples staged before the source guard and any future writer. Receipt samples (no outcome; they come only from successful tool calls) stay trainable. Test: failed_mission_outcomes_are_never_trainable (FAILED/BLOCKED skipped; COMPLETE/SUCCESS/receipt/no-metadata kept; an all-failure batch errors naming the reason).

The Tier-0 input projection no longer merges unrelated words. Before: SusiAlphaModel::get_semantic_anchor hashed each non-category word by summing its bytes, so every anagram (stop/post/pots/tops/spot/opts) and every equal-sum word lit the same bucket and was one feature to the reflex classifier. The same projection feeds fleet recruitment's goal-vs-agent cosine (susi-gawd-agents agents/fleet.rs, threshold 0.35), so those collisions also inflated recruitment similarity. Now the bucket comes from order-sensitive FNV-1a. Category anchors and the bucket weight are unchanged. No checkpoint migration is needed: the EV-CLAUDE-002 held-out gate scores both the active and the candidate weights under the current projection, so a stale checkpoint is judged honestly and replaced on the next training cycle. Test: anagrams_project_to_distinct_features (at least 5 distinct buckets for 6 anagrams; category synonyms still coincide).

Tier-0 reflex training no longer forgets earlier batches. Before: each cycle loaded the active weights and trained 100 epochs on only the claimed batch plus vocabulary primes, so knowledge from earlier batches was overwritten (catastrophic forgetting). Now a bounded replay set sits beside the checkpoint (<weights>.replay.jsonl, REPLAY_CAPACITY 2048 most-recent distinct intents). Samples are stored by action name, so they survive vocabulary growth, and are dropped if their action leaves the vocabulary. The newest label wins when an intent is restaged with a different action. Every cycle trains, and gates, on claim plus replay. Because is_holdout is stable per intent, replayed held-out samples turn the EV-CLAUDE-002 gate into a forgetting check as well. The replay set is saved only after a checkpoint publishes, so a held-back cycle leaves it untouched. The merge is linear (reverse pass + HashSet). Tests: replay_merge_keeps_newest_label_and_bounded_recency; replay_load_tolerates_missing_and_torn_files; prior_cycles_are_replayed_into_later_training (cycle 1 teaches 'zorblat quux' -> reason; after cycle 2 trains only 'show the content' -> read_file, the report says 'Replayed 3 prior sample(s)' and the model still predicts reason for 'zorblat quux'). It and the gate test passed 8 of 8 repeated runs.

The Tier-0 reflex classifier no longer lets a leading category word hijack unrelated prompts. Measured before the change, after training on 12 everyday samples: 'write a poem about the ocean' was classified write_file at 0.84 confidence, above SusiPulse's 0.5 serve bar, so Tier-0 would answer a poem request with a file-write action. The cause was the input projection. semantic_centroid_projection lights a 10-dim band at 1.0 for a category word but one dim at 0.5 for any other word, and weights the first word most, so the poem prompt sat at cosine 0.992 to 'write notes to todo.md'. Now the classifier (training, held-out gate, prediction) uses SusiAlphaModel::reflex_features: stopwords dropped, every word equal norm and position-independent, category words spread over their band, other words over two seeded FNV-1a buckets. Fleet recruitment keeps semantic_centroid_projection, which its 0.35 threshold is tuned to; the hashing was factored into anchor_category and fnv1a. Measured after, same data: the poem prompt is at 0.40 (not served), all 7 out-of-distribution probes are below 0.5, and in-distribution prompts score 0.71-0.89. Tests: reflex_features_weigh_content_words_like_the_verb (deterministic: poem vs write-notes cosine < 0.6, stopword/order invariance, unit norm); leading_category_word_no_longer_hijacks_unrelated_prompts (4 out-of-distribution prompts refused, in-distribution served; alpha suite passed 10 of 10 runs). Existing checkpoints migrate through the EV-CLAUDE-002 gate, which scores active and candidate weights under the current features.

Tier-0 reflexes are served only for prompts the model has support for. The classifier has no abstain class: every prompt maps to some action, and confidence was the only guard against serving a canned action for something it never trained on. Now a loaded SusiAlphaModel carries the reflex features of its replay set (n x 128, flattened). predict_intent refuses when the nearest trained intent is below cosine SUPPORT_MIN (0.6), before it consults confidence (still > 0.5). Calibration from measurements on everyday training data: out-of-distribution probes are <= 0.52, and a paraphrase sharing two of three content words is about 0.67. Checkpoints without a replay set (bootstrap, pre-replay) keep the confidence-only gate; support() returns None for them. The replay file is now written before the bundle publishes, because the bundle mtime keys SusiAlphaModel::cached and a cached model must not hold a stale support set. Cost: at most 2048 x 128 multiply-adds per uncached prompt. Test: unfamiliar_prompts_are_refused_even_when_confident (paraphrase support > 0.9; the poem prompt below 0.6 is refused with 'Unfamiliar prompt'; no replay gives None). The alpha suite passed 5 of 5 repeated runs.

Reflex training outcomes are now visible, and a held-back claim backs off. Before: amas.rs runs ReflexTrainer::audit_distillation_state on a background thread after every supervised mission and discards the result. Once the EV-CLAUDE-002 gate could refuse a checkpoint, that meant (a) held-back and failed cycles were invisible, and (b) the restored claim was refit and refused again on every following mission. Now train_claim (shared by audit and force_train) logs each cycle to <ws>/.susi/distillation_log.jsonl: timestamp, outcome published/held_back/error, claim size, credential-redacted report; bounded to 200 entries and written under the training-cycle lock. A log-write failure never fails the cycle. held_back_wait makes the automatic audit defer after a held_back until the staged count reaches the held-back claim size + reflex_training_threshold; force_train bypasses it. Held-back detection matches the GEMI error prefix 'reflex checkpoint held back' (HELD_BACK_MARKER) because the error crosses the plane bus as a string; the producer side is commented and its test asserts the marker. Tests: cycle_log_is_bounded_and_newest_last; held_back_cycle_defers_until_enough_new_samples (threshold 50, held back at 60: 60 and 109 staged defer, 110 trains; published or absent history never defers).

Operators can see Tier-0 distillation health. susi substrate status now includes reflexes.distillation, from susi_gawd::reflex_trainer::distillation_summary, which reads <ws>/.susi/distillation_log.jsonl (EV-CLAUDE-008): cycle counts by outcome (published / held_back / error) and the most recent cycle record. Before, held-back or failed training cycles were visible only in the log file. Verified on a dev build (target/debug/susi, isolated HOME resolving to .susi-dev, release ~/.susi untouched): with a scratch workspace holding one published and one held_back cycle, the command printed cycles=2, published=1, held_back=1, and last.outcome=held_back with its report. Test: summary_counts_outcomes_and_shows_the_last_cycle. The lanes board also records an open question for Devin's mission layer: a reflex_served field on traces would let distill suppress and unlearn reflexes that led to failed missions, which is not joinable today.

Tier-0 no longer trains on contradictory labels. Before: ReceiptArchive stages mission goal -> tool name for every successful tool call (capture.rs passes the session goal as training_intent). So one multi-tool mission staged the same intent under several labels (read_file, write_file, run_test_harness, ...), and the classifier was fit toward all of them at once. After EV-CLAUDE-005 the replay merge's newest-wins rule would have crowned whichever tool ran last. Now parse_training_entries runs resolve_label_conflicts over each batch: per normalized intent, the samples are kept only for a label holding a strict majority of that intent's samples, and all are dropped (counted as skipped, 'no majority label') when none does. Repeated single-tool missions still teach; multi-tool goals, which no single reflex action could serve, do not. Test: conflicting_labels_keep_only_a_strict_majority (a 1-1 split is dropped; 2-of-3 keeps the majority samples and drops the minority; the unique intent is kept; skipped=3).

Tier-0 fits run to convergence, so a grown reflex model can actually serve. Measured before (scratch probe, 962 training samples over 20 actions, fresh init): the fixed 100 full-batch AdamW steps reached 95.3% argmax accuracy on the training set but loss was still 1.597. 0.0% of samples were both correct and above SusiPulse's 0.5 serve confidence, so the model was right yet refused everything. At 200 steps 91.9% were served, at 300 steps 94.2%, with held-out accuracy flat at about 0.92 (no overfitting cost). Now ReflexNet::fit trains until mean loss <= TARGET_LOSS (0.15, correct class ~0.86) or MAX_EPOCHS (600), returns (epochs, loss), and the training report states both. Small batches still stop early. Test: fit_trains_to_serving_confidence_at_realistic_scale (900 samples / 20 actions: more than 100 epochs needed, at least 80% correct and above the serve bar). The alpha suite passed 6 of 6 repeated runs; its runtime rose from about 3s to 10s.

Tools that are actually used can become Tier-0 reflexes even when the vocabulary is full. Before: the 128-slot action vocabulary was seeded with the 9 foundational intents plus agents and tools sorted alphabetically and truncated (list_dynamic_intents), and extend_vocabulary stopped once 128 was reached. A newly installed or late-alphabet tool therefore stayed outside the vocabulary, and parse_training_entries skipped its samples on every cycle. The defaults alone are 9 + 52 agents, so more than 67 tools saturates the vocabulary. Now train_on_staged_file runs admit_staged_actions before parsing. For each action named by non-failed staged lines that is a real capability (capability_names, untruncated: agents + tools, foundational excluded), it appends while there is room, and otherwise reclaims the highest-index slot that is not foundational, has no training support (absent from the replay set), and is not wanted by this batch. Slot indices of all other actions are unchanged, the reused output row is refit in the same cycle, and the report lists 'old -> new' reclaims. Non-capability labels never take a slot. Test: full_vocabulary_reclaims_unsupported_slots_for_used_capabilities (full 128-vocab: two used capabilities take the two highest unsupported filler slots; a supported slot, the foundational intents and all other indices are untouched; a non-capability is refused; with room left, capabilities are appended without reclaiming). Known bias: the held-out gate scores the active checkpoint on reused indices under their new meaning; the old action had no support, so the active model rarely predicts it.

The distill stage is proven end to end across process-plane boundaries, not only per crate. New integration test tests/distill_loop_tests.rs::staged_successes_train_publish_and_serve_a_tier0_reflex. It isolates HOME, USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME to a temp root, sets SUSI_TEST_MOCK_INFERENCE, and wires planes with susi_daemon::composition::wire_plane_bus plus the SusiEngineHooks the CLI and daemon use. It then (1) stages 54 successful pairs through the production writer ProtocolKnowledgeBase::stage_distillation_pair, plus one FAILED pair that must not teach; (2) runs ReflexTrainer::audit_distillation_state, which claims the buffer and trains over the plane bus (GEMI_ALPHA_TRAIN) through the held-out gate and publication; (3) asserts the report says distillation completed, the staging buffer was consumed, and distillation_summary shows published=1; (4) loads the published checkpoint from the isolated config dir and asserts it predicts 'ACTION: list_directory' for 'list files in src' with support > 0.9; (5) asserts SusiPulse::reason serves 'ACTION: list_directory ...' from Tier-0. It passed 3 of 3 runs, about 1.7s each. It runs in CI's root-cli shard (-p susi).

Fixes a Tier-0 availability regression introduced by EV-CLAUDE-007: support_matrix propagated a replay-file read error with '?', so a replay set that existed but could not be read (permissions, a directory in its place, I/O fault) failed the checkpoint load for every candidate generation and disabled Tier-0 entirely. Now support_matrix returns Option: no replay set or an unreadable one both yield None, which is the confidence-only gate, and the unreadable case constructs an EaiError::io so the degradation reaches the error-metrics sink. Training still errors on an unreadable replay set, which is visible in the distillation log. Test extension in unfamiliar_prompts_are_refused_even_when_confident: the replay file is replaced by a directory, the trained checkpoint still loads, support() is None, and predict_intent still serves 'ACTION: list_directory' for the familiar prompt.

Tier-0 training is class-balanced, so a dominant action no longer swallows rare ones. Measured with ReflexNet on 454 samples (one action with 400 samples, nine with 6 each) and 36 unseen combinations of seen words for the minority actions, over 5 random inits each. Plain mean NLL: 1-11 of 36 correct, 0 correct-and-served, and 13-28 confidently (>0.5) served the majority action. Class-balanced: 34-36 of 36 correct, 29-35 correct-and-served, and 0-2 wrong-but-served. Now ReflexNet::fit takes per-sample weights and minimizes the weighted mean of -log p(label), computed with gather over log-softmax. Training and the held-out candidate use fit_weights: staged samples weigh n/(K*n_c) (class_balance_weights; weights sum to n), and each synthetic prime weighs 1. A prime balanced as a class of one would outweigh every real sample of a contradicting label sharing its features; this was caught by regressing_checkpoint_is_held_back_and_improving_one_publishes failing 8/8 before primes were excluded. Tests: class_balance_weights_equalize_class_mass; a_majority_action_does_not_swallow_minority_actions (asserts >= 30/36 correct and <= 4 wrong-but-served). The alpha suite passed 8 of 8 repeated runs. An earlier variant of the probe, with two unseen words out of three, was too noisy to gate on (1-7/9 correct balanced) and was replaced by this one.

The Tier-0 publication gate now measures the error that serving actually risks. Before, holdout_gate compared argmax accuracy only, so a candidate with equal held-out accuracy but more confident mistakes (wrong argmax with probability above the serve bar, which predict_intent would hand out as a reflex) passed. Now ReflexNet::evaluate returns Evaluation { correct, wrong_served }. Probabilities are the softmax over every output, as predict_intent computes them; the argmax is taken within the model's vocabulary; wrong_served counts wrong argmaxes above SERVE_CONFIDENCE (0.5, now a named constant that predict_intent also uses). The gate refuses publication when candidate.correct < active.correct or candidate.wrong_served > active.wrong_served, and the report and held-back error state both numbers for both models. The test-only correct() helper was removed in favour of evaluate(). Test: evaluation_counts_confident_mistakes_as_served (a confident prediction scored against its own label is correct; against another label it is a served mistake; with a vocabulary that cannot express it, it is a low-probability miss, not served). The alpha suite passed 5 of 5 runs.

Fixes a retrain livelock in the distill stage. Before: when a claimed batch held nothing trainable (every line a failed outcome, a label outside the vocabulary that is not a capability, or a blank intent), GEMI's parse_training_entries returned 'No trainable distillation records' and ReflexTrainer restored the claim like any other error. Only held_back cycles backed off, so every following mission (amas.rs runs the audit after each one) re-claimed, re-failed and restored the same lines, while distillation_staged.jsonl kept growing. Now train_claim matches UNTRAINABLE_MARKERS ('No trainable distillation records', 'Empty distillation dataset'; the producer side in alpha.rs is commented as a contract), retires the claim, logs the cycle as 'untrainable', and returns Ok with a 'Retired N untrainable staged sample(s)' report. held_back_wait now also backs off after an 'error' cycle (waits for claim size + threshold new samples) but not after 'untrainable'. distillation_summary counts 'untrainable'. Tests: held_back_cycle_defers_until_enough_new_samples (extended: an error cycle defers; an untrainable cycle does not); tests/distill_loop_tests.rs::an_untrainable_claim_is_retired_not_retried_forever (55 non-capability samples through the production writer, audit over the plane bus: report says 'Retired 55 untrainable', staging buffer consumed, summary untrainable=1, error=0). The integration file passed 3 of 3 runs.

The distillation staging buffer is now bounded, completing the roadmap's append-only boundedness sweep for the distill stage. Before: distillation_staged.jsonl shrank only when a training cycle published. Restored claims plus new arrivals meant a persistently failing trainer, even with the EV-CLAUDE-017 back-off, grew it by about one threshold's worth per retry with no upper bound, and every audit read the whole file. Now claim_staged_samples runs cap_claimed_buffer after sanitizing: a claim keeps the newest STAGING_CAP (20,000) valid lines, rewritten atomically, and the drop count is recorded as an EaiError::io in the error-metrics sink. The claim's sample_count is the kept count, so back-off arithmetic stays consistent. Test: claimed_buffer_keeps_only_the_newest_samples_over_cap (at cap: unchanged; over cap: exactly the newest 3 of 10 kept, in order).

Closes a latent code-execution hole in the verify stage. verification.rs documented that contracts which could mutate state are refused as Unverifiable before any process spawns. But the CommandExit allowlist included sh and bash with any arguments, so sh -c 'rm -rf .' was a valid probe, and git and cargo were allowed with any subcommand (git push, git checkout ., cargo install/publish). It was latent: no production code constructs CommandExit today (contracts_from_text mines only FileExists/FileAbsent, and the truth.rs callers use those). But Contract is pub + Deserialize, so the first code that mined or accepted a CommandExit from mission text or model output would have gained arbitrary execution. Now verifier_policy decides per program: pure readers (test, cmp, diff, grep, sha256sum, true, false, cat, ls, wc) with any arguments; git only status/diff/log/show/rev-parse/ls-files; cargo only test/check/build/clippy, or fmt with --check; no shells. Refusal returns Unverifiable before spawning, and the message still says 'allowlist'. Test: verifier_policy_refuses_shells_and_mutating_subcommands (10 refused and 6 allowed argvs; a refused 'sh -c touch marker' leaves no marker). Existing verification tests pass (8/8).

Deletion claims can no longer be verified about paths outside the workspace. Before: Contract::FileAbsent computed root.join(path). An absolute path replaces the root under Path::join, and '..' climbs out of it, so a claim like 'deleted /nonexistent/x' or 'deleted ../x' whose target did not exist fell through canonicalize()'s error arm and returned Verified ('no filesystem entry'). That is a verified claim about state the registry does not govern. An existing escaped path was already Violated; only nonexistent escapes slipped through. Now FileAbsent returns Unverifiable ('not workspace-relative') for any absolute path or any path with a ParentDir component, before touching the filesystem. Test: file_absent_never_vouches_for_paths_outside_the_workspace (/nonexistent/..., ../sibling, sub/../../escape are all Unverifiable); the existing file_absent_distinguishes_gone_present_and_escaped still passes (9/9 verification tests).

Tier 1 (the embedded qwen2.5-0.5b generative reflex behind Tier-0) no longer wastes a generation, and no longer serves an empty action. Before, in SusiPulse::reason: GenerativeReflexEngine::try_solve ran a greedy generation of up to 64 tokens and always returned format!("ACTION: {}"). Pulse's starts_with("ACTION:") check was therefore always true, so it immediately ran try_generate_answer (up to 256 tokens) and used the routing output only if that failed. If try_solve failed, a 'Tier 2' block called try_generate_answer again on the same model. The routing generation was wasted on every Tier-1 reflex that produced an answer, and a missing model was tried redundantly. Also, an empty routing decode returned Ok('ACTION: '), which was served and cached as a solve. Now pulse::generative_tiers runs the answer first and the ACTION routing only on failure, with the same outcomes in every case, and try_solve returns Err (task marked failed) when the decoded action is empty. Test: tier1_generates_an_answer_first_and_routes_only_on_failure (answer served with zero routing calls; routing used when the answer fails; both failing is Err). Latency saving: one greedy generation of up to 64 tokens per Tier-1 reflex; not benchmarked here because the reflex model is not provisioned in the test environment.

Tier-0 reflex quality now has a standing regression benchmark instead of only per-change probes. alpha::tests::tier0_benchmark_recall_precision_and_ood_refusal trains through the production train_on_staged_file path on BENCH_TRAIN (90 phrasings, 10 per foundational intent: status, version, self_heal_build, run_test_harness, write_file, read_file, list_directory, scout, reason). It loads the published checkpoint and scores it through predict_intent, with both confidence and support gates, on BENCH_TEST (27 unseen paraphrases) and BENCH_OOD (20 everyday non-command prompts such as 'what is the capital of france', 'write a poem about the ocean', 'delete everything in production'). Baseline measured before the test was written, over 3 random inits: recall 26/27, 27/27 and 26/27; served precision 100% in every run; OOD served 0/20 in every run. The single miss was 'show version': support 0.95 but confidence 0.46-0.48, so it was refused rather than served wrong. Assertions: recall >= 24/27, wrong serves <= 1, OOD serves <= 1. The alpha suite passed 6 of 6 repeated runs.

Tier-0 recall improves without giving up precision or out-of-distribution refusal. The EV-CLAUDE-022 benchmark's only miss was 'show version': support 0.95, meaning a near-duplicate of a trained intent, but confidence 0.46-0.48, just under the 0.5 serve bar, so it was refused. Now the support set remembers each replayed row's action (SupportSet { features, actions }), and SusiAlphaModel::nearest returns the nearest trained intent's cosine and action. predict_intent keeps the support gate (cosine >= 0.6), then serves when alpha::serves holds: confidence > SERVE_CONFIDENCE (0.5), or confidence > AGREED_CONFIDENCE (0.35) with the nearest trained intent at cosine >= NEIGHBOR_AGREEMENT (0.9) and carrying the predicted action (case-insensitive). The two independent signals, classifier and nearest example, must agree. Measured on the benchmark over 5 random inits: recall 27/27 in 5 of 5 (was 26-27/27), 0 wrong serves, 0/20 OOD served. The benchmark's recall bound was raised from 24 to 25. Test: low_confidence_serves_only_with_an_agreeing_near_duplicate (confident alone; no support set -> confidence only; agreeing near-duplicate serves; disagreeing neighbor, cosine 0.85, or confidence 0.30 do not). The alpha suite passed 5 of 5 runs.

Tier-1 generated answers are no longer served stale from the reflex cache. Before: SusiPulse cached every served reflex keyed by (workspace, prompt) and cleared the cache only when the Tier-0 model fingerprint changed, which happens only on a Tier-0 publish. Tier-0 entries are deterministic action mappings, so that invalidation is right for them. Tier-1 entries are text generated by the 0.5B reflex LLM for prompts like 'what's the weather', and could be re-served verbatim for as long as the Tier-0 model stayed unchanged, possibly days. Now cache entries carry an optional expiry (CachedReflex = (String, Option<Instant>)): Tier-0 actions None (fingerprint-invalidated as before), Tier-1 answers now + TIER1_CACHE_TTL (600s). cache_lookup refuses expired entries. Test: generated_answers_expire_but_model_actions_do_not (Tier-1 answer served before the deadline and refused after; the Tier-0 action is still served after). The existing bound and workspace-separation cache tests still pass.

Removes a per-mission I/O cost from the learning loop. amas.rs runs ReflexTrainer::audit_distillation_state on a background thread after every supervised mission and discards the result. Its most common outcome, 'no training due' (below threshold) or 'deferred' (back-off), appended staging_health_line. That calls ReceiptArchive::staging_health_summary -> load_audit_lines, which reads and JSON-parses every receipt-archive generation (live plus KEEP_GENERATIONS rotated files, up to 8 x 16 MB per the roadmap's receipt-archive bound), all to build a string nobody reads. Now the not-due and back-off decisions go through due_claim(workspace, threshold), which does only the cheap checks: the distillation log tail and the staging file. The not-due report is one line with no archive scan. Cycles that actually train, and force_train, still report staging health. Test: nothing_due_claims_nothing_and_backs_off (below threshold: no claim and the buffer untouched; after a held_back at 6 with threshold 5: no claim at 6 staged; at 11 staged: claims all 11).

Tier-0 serving no longer rewrites actions that merely contain 'list_directory'. SusiPulse::reason rewrote any served Tier-0 action whose text contained the substring 'list_directory' into 'ACTION: list_directory <workspace>'. With EV-CLAUDE-012 vocabulary reclamation, arbitrary installed tools can become Tier-0 labels, so a tool named e.g. list_directory_tree, or anything containing that name, would have been served as a different action. Now pulse::bind_workspace rewrites only the exact 'ACTION: list_directory' and passes every other action through unchanged. Test: only_the_list_directory_action_is_bound_to_the_workspace (exact action bound to /w; list_directory_tree, status and my_list_directory unchanged). The end-to-end distill-loop test, which asserts the served 'ACTION: list_directory ...', still passes.

Operators can see the Tier-0 model itself, not only its training log. SusiAlphaModel::inventory(global_dir) returns the active checkpoint filename (via the bundle manifest, falling back to the previous generation as load does), vocabulary size against the 128-slot capacity (reclamation starts when full, EV-CLAUDE-012), replay-set sample count and distinct replayed actions. It is read-only: unlike load(), it never publishes a bootstrap model. susi substrate status shows it as reflexes.tier0 next to reflexes.distillation. Verified on a dev build (target/debug/susi) with an isolated HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME: it printed checkpoint null, vocabulary 0, capacity 128, replay 0, and no .safetensors file was created. Test: inventory_reports_checkpoint_vocabulary_and_replay (an empty dir reports nothing and creates no models dir; after training on 12 samples over 6 actions it reports a .safetensors checkpoint, vocabulary >= 9, capacity 128, replay_samples 12, replay_actions 6).

Write goals with a quoted content literal are now verified by content, not only existence. SusiTruthAgent::verify_mission_reality upgraded a goal's write contract from FileExists to FileContains only when the goal used a colon ('containing: <text>' / 'containing exactly: <text>'). A goal like 'Create a file named q.txt containing "payload-7"' therefore passed verification with any content in q.txt. The colon was a deliberate precision guard: unquoted prose such as 'containing the results of the analysis' is a description, not a literal. A quoted string is as explicit as the colon form. Now GOAL_CONTENT also accepts containing (exactly)? followed by a "..."/'...'/`...` literal, and unquoted prose without a colon still yields an existence contract. Test: quoted_containing_literal_is_a_content_contract_prose_is_not (wrong content violates the quoted literal; correct content passes; the prose goal passes with arbitrary content). The existing colon-form tests pass (16/16 truth tests).

Tier-0 training can no longer have its locks broken mid-cycle. FileLock::is_stale treats a lock older than 60s as a wedged holder even when the holder pid is alive, which is by design, because its guarded sections are meant to be millisecond-scale. The trainer holds two locks far longer: the workspace 'reflex_claim_training' cycle lock across the whole plane-bus training call, and GEMI's global 'reflex_training' lock across train_on_staged_file. Measured (scratch probe, debug build): a first cycle at 2057 samples took 7.4s for 168 epochs, about 44ms per epoch. A non-converging gated cycle is two fits of up to 600 epochs, about 53s, close to 60s. Past that, the next mission's background audit could break the cycle lock and recover_orphaned_claims would restore the live claim into staging while it trains (duplicated samples, then a retire_claim failure), or a second trainer could break the training lock and publish over the cycle. Now FileLock::refresh (mtime = now) and FileLock::hold_while run the work while a heartbeat thread refreshes every 20s. Both trainer locks (ReflexTrainer::audit_distillation_state / force_train around train_claim, and SusiAlphaModel::train_on_staged_file around train_locked) use it. FileLock's staleness rule for every other caller is unchanged. Tests (susi-config, new): refresh_keeps_a_long_live_holder_from_going_stale (a 2-minute-old lock is stale, after refresh it is not); hold_while_returns_the_work_result_and_keeps_the_lock (still exclusive inside, result returned, released after drop). Trainer, alpha and distill-loop suites pass.

Claim mining no longer carries prose punctuation into verified paths, which caused errors in both directions. contracts_from_text takes the token after 'wrote to'/'saved to'/'deleted'/'removed' as a bare path and trimmed only trailing '.,;'. Measured before the fix: 'I saved to notes.txt: done' mined notes.txt:, '(saved to out/report.md)' mined out/report.md), 'I wrote to report.md!' mined report.md!, and 'wrote to data.json)' mined data.json). Each FileExists then failed, so truthful write claims became TRUTH_VIOLATION governance errors. On the deletion side, 'removed old.log)' mined FileAbsent{old.log)}, a path that never exists, so the deletion verified while old.log was still present. Now trim_bare_path strips leading ([{ and trailing .,;:!?)]}"'` from bare paths; quoted and backticked paths are still taken verbatim. Test: bare_claim_paths_shed_surrounding_prose_punctuation (5 write phrasings mine the clean path; 'Done (removed old.log)' mines old.log and is Violated while old.log exists; a backticked path with a space is kept). Verification 10/10 and truth 16/16 tests pass.

Iteration 1 — trace schema v2: tools are real tools. emit_mission_trace now populates MissionTrace.tools from the EvidenceSession's ToolReceipts (falling back to capability-registered interaction actions when no session bound the mission); interaction actions moved to a bounded signals field. Previously tools collected supervision labels (MISSION_FLUX, PLAN_SEARCH, CLOUD_ATTEMPT_*), so failing_tools() could veto control-flow tokens and briefs described control flow, not capabilities. evidence_entries now counts receipts when a session exists.
entries.proof: mission_trace tests now 8 (v1-without-signals parse regression). susi-core 206, susi-gawd-swarm 54 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 2 — proven-tool steering in plan scoring. mission_trace::proven_tools returns tools that appear only on successful similar missions (ambiguous = also-failed earns nothing); deliberation::score_plan_with_history rewards each mention +0.05 (capped at 4 so keyword stuffing cannot win). HistorySignals bundles failed+proven into one scoring input — deliberate() now takes five args again (clippy too_many_arguments). The planner now steers toward what worked, not only away from what failed.
entries.proof: Tests: proven_tools_flags_only_unambiguous_successes (ambiguous exclusion), proven_history_tools_reward_but_stay_capped (bonus + cap). susi-core 207, susi-gawd-swarm 55 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 3 — candidate dedup with consensus-ordering fix. Identical decompositions from different budgets dedup to one execution candidate (post-sort, keeping the best-scored variant). Consensus is measured pre-dedup: two budgets independently producing the same plan is the strongest agreement signal and collapsing it first would silently withhold approval from mutating intents. Score ties deterministically prefer the shorter plan.
entries.proof: deliberation::tests now 8 — duplicate_plans_dedup_and_ties_prefer_fewer_steps plus the consensus regression both covered. susi-gawd-swarm 56 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 4 — unverified-mutation penalty. When the intent demands consensus (Mutate/SelfExtend scope or High+ risk), a candidate carrying zero verifiable steps loses 0.20 on its score with a rationale marker; read-scope plans are exempt. A blind mutation is now outscored by one that checks its own work.
entries.proof: deliberation tests now 10: mutating_intents_penalize_plans_without_verification, read_scope_plans_skip_the_unverified_penalty. susi-gawd-swarm 58 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 5 — repetition-scaled failure penalties. mission_trace::failing_tool_counts returns tool→failed-mission-count maps (ambiguous still excluded); score_plan_with_history docks each mention 0.10 per past failure, capped at 3 occurrences (max -0.30/mention). A tool that failed three similar missions now visibly outranks a one-off flake. failing_tools() kept as the set view for existing callers.
entries.proof: Tests: repeated_failures_dock_harder_than_one_offs (monotonic + cap), counts asserted in failing_tools test. susi-core 207, susi-gawd-swarm 59 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Mission planning can no longer be answered by a reflex tier. ama::master::plan_steps sent the decomposition prompt ('Break the following goal into at most N concise, ordered steps... Goal: <goal> Steps:') through GemiEngine::generate_reasoning, which allows both reflex tiers. Measured with reflex_features: the template around the goal 'check system status health report' scores cosine 0.720 against the bare goal ('check system status' 0.566, 'list files in src' 0.497). So once Tier-0 had trained on such a goal, the planning request cleared the 0.6 support gate and could be served 'ACTION: status'. The step parser keeps only numbered lines, so it dropped that line, and the mission silently fell back to a single-step plan. Tier-1 could likewise answer planning with the 0.5B reflex model. plan_steps now calls generate_reasoning_deep (allow_reflex=false). This was posted as an open question on docs/brain-lanes.md for Devin's lane and applied here, flagged in the commit, while master.rs was clean on Devin's side. The board marks it resolved. susi-gawd-swarm tests pass (59/59).

Bare action names are served by Tier-0 instead of refused as unfamiliar. Every vocabulary action is trained on a synthetic prime, its own name, so the classifier knows 'scout' means scout. But the EV-CLAUDE-007 support set held only replayed intents, so a bare 'scout', 'version' or 'reason' was refused whenever that exact wording had never been staged: its features lit a band no replayed intent touched, giving support 0.0. Now support_matrix(weights_path, vocabulary) appends one support row per vocabulary action (the name, labelled with itself) to the replay rows. The rows exist only when a replay set exists, so pre-replay checkpoints keep the legacy gate. Measured after training on 6 samples covering status/list_directory/read_file/self_heal_build/run_test_harness: bare 'status', 'scout', 'version', 'reason', 'read file' and 'list directory' all had support 1.0 and served the matching action; 'hi' (support 0.0) and 'joke' (0.22) were refused. Test: bare_action_names_are_supported_by_their_primes (after EVERYDAY training, which never stages scout or reason: both have support > 0.99 and serve their action; 'tell me a joke' is refused). The alpha suite, including the Tier-0 benchmark, passed 5 of 5 runs.

Tier-0 no longer serves negated or destructive prompts as the opposite action. Measured on the Tier-0 benchmark model (trained on BENCH_TRAIN) before the guard, 16 adversarial prompts: 'delete the config file' -> write_file (support 0.77), 'remove all files' -> list_directory (0.81), 'overwrite the readme file' -> write_file, "don't read the file" -> read_file (0.71), 'never list files' -> list_directory (0.89), 'shutdown the system' -> status (0.78), 'do not run the tests' -> run_test_harness (0.83), 'stop the build' -> version (0.71). The rest were already refused by the support or confidence gates. The reflex features are a bag of words, so negation and destructive verbs are invisible to them. Now the support set also records, per action, the lowercased words it was trained with (replay intents plus its own name). predict_intent refuses ('Vetoed: ...') when the prompt contains a VETO_WORDS entry (negation/reversal: not, no, never, don/dont/doesn/didn/isn, without, except, stop, cancel, avoid, skip, undo, revert, rollback; destructive/control: delete, remove, rm, erase, wipe, drop, destroy, purge, truncate, kill, shutdown, reboot, uninstall, format, reset, overwrite) that the predicted action was never trained with. An action truly taught 'delete the build cache' still serves it. Legacy checkpoints without a support set are unaffected. Test: negated_and_destructive_prompts_are_vetoed_unless_learned (the 7 previously mis-served prompts are refused; vetoed_word allows a learned 'delete' for self_heal_build and flags 'delete' for write_file). The Tier-0 benchmark and the alpha suite passed 5 of 5 runs.

Tier-0 no longer serves actions that nothing can execute. Vocabulary slots persist after a tool or agent is uninstalled (EV-CLAUDE-012 reclamation only reuses an unsupported slot later, and a trained slot keeps its weights), so a model could confidently serve 'ACTION: <uninstalled_tool>' and the mission then failed downstream. Now predict_intent requires action_available(action): the action is a FOUNDATIONAL_INTENTS entry or a currently registered agent/tool name (SusiAlphaModel::capability_names), compared case-insensitively. The capability set is snapshotted for 30s (AVAILABILITY_TTL) behind an RwLock so serving does not rescan the registries per prompt. Refusal message: '<action> is no longer an installed capability; not served as a reflex.' Test: only_foundational_or_installed_actions_are_servable (all 9 foundational intents servable, case-insensitive; an unknown tool is not). The alpha suite passed 3 of 3 runs and the end-to-end distill-loop test passes.

Over-long intents no longer enter Tier-0 training. ReceiptArchive stages each successful receipt with the session's whole (redacted) mission goal as the intent, with no length bound; mission traces bound goals to 240 chars (MAX_GOAL_CHARS). A multi-paragraph goal therefore became a replay intent. It inflated the 2048-entry replay file, and after EV-CLAUDE-033 it would have diluted the action's learned veto-word vocabulary with every incidental word in the goal ('delete', 'stop', ...), weakening the veto guard. Now parse_training_entries skips intents longer than MAX_REFLEX_INTENT_CHARS (240, the trace goal bound) as untrainable, counted in skipped. Skipping rather than truncating is deliberate, because a truncated goal is a different sentence. Test: over_long_intents_are_not_reflex_samples (a 300-char intent is skipped; the short one is kept). Alpha suite 36/36.

Closes a cache bypass of EV-CLAUDE-034. SusiPulse::reason returns reflex-cache hits before reaching predict_intent, and Tier-0 cache entries have no time expiry (they are invalidated only by a Tier-0 model fingerprint change). So an 'ACTION: <tool>' cached while the tool was installed would keep being served after the tool was uninstalled, until the next Tier-0 publish. Now a cache hit whose value is a Tier-0 action is served only if pulse::still_servable holds, which reuses alpha::action_available (now pub(crate), backed by the 30s capability snapshot) on the action name, ignoring bound arguments such as list_directory's workspace. Otherwise the entry is evicted and resolution continues to the live tiers. Tier-1 free-text answers are unaffected (they expire by TTL, EV-CLAUDE-024). Test: cached_actions_must_still_be_runnable (list_directory with a path, status, and a Tier-1 text are servable; an uninstalled tool with args is not). Pulse tests 6/6.

The per-mission distillation audit reads nothing in its common case. After EV-CLAUDE-025 the not-due path no longer parsed the receipt archive, but due_claim still read the whole staging buffer twice after every supervised mission (held_back_wait's staged count, then claim_staged_samples' count), and the buffer can reach several MB near the 20k-sample cap. Now due_claim first stats the file. If its size is below threshold x MIN_STAGED_RECORD_BYTES (40, the exact size of the smallest possible record: a JSON object with intent/action/timestamp keys, empty values, and a newline), it cannot hold threshold samples and the audit returns without reading. The bound is sound because every writer emits at least those three keys. Test: the_smallest_real_record_meets_the_size_bound (the minimal record is >= 40 bytes); nothing_due_claims_nothing_and_backs_off still passes. The trainer unit suite (16/16) and the end-to-end distill-loop test pass.

Content and hash verification no longer loads whole files into memory. Contract::FileContains and Contract::FileHash called std::fs::read on the confined file, so a mission claiming a large artifact (a multi-GB dump or log with a hash or content claim) made the verifier allocate the entire file. Now stream_contains reads 64 KiB chunks (STREAM_CHUNK) and keeps the last needle.len()-1 bytes as carry-over, so a needle spanning a chunk boundary is still found; an empty needle is verified when the file is readable, as before. stream_sha256 feeds chunks into an incremental Sha256. Verdicts and messages are unchanged: unreadable or unconfined still yields the 'not an existing regular workspace file' violation. Test: streamed_checks_find_boundary_spanning_content_and_match_digests (a needle straddling the first 64 KiB boundary of a 192 KiB file is found; a missing needle is not; empty needle true; an absent file None; the streamed digest equals the one-shot SHA-256). Verification 11/11 and truth 16/16 tests pass.

Failed missions stop teaching Tier-0 through their tool receipts. EV-CLAUDE-003 filtered mission-trace samples by outcome, but receipt samples (ReceiptArchive: goal -> tool for each successful tool call) are staged at tool-call time, before the mission's outcome exists. A mission that ultimately failed still taught goal -> tool for every tool call that individually succeeded. Now ReflexTrainer::train_claim first runs drop_failed_mission_receipts. It reads the workspace's mission traces (mission_trace::read_all; the latest trace per mission_id wins) and removes claimed samples whose performance_metadata.source is tool_receipt and whose receipt_id session matches a trace recorded as not succeeded. The receipt id is '<session>:<index>' or '<session>:r-<nanos>' (capture.rs), and report.rs writes the trace's mission_id from the same EvidenceSession id. Receipts with no trace yet (outcome unknown) and non-receipt samples are kept; if nothing is left, the claim is retired as untrainable (EV-CLAUDE-017). Test: receipts_from_failed_missions_are_dropped_before_training (traces ok-session COMPLETE and bad-session FAILED; of 5 lines, both bad-session receipts, local and remote id forms, are dropped; ok, unknown and trace samples are kept). Trainer suite 17/17.

Tier-0 serving latency cut about 6.5x, restoring margin under the sub-2ms reflex mandate that ReflexEngine audits as LATENCY_VIOLATION. Measured in a release build with a 2,057-row support set (2,100 staged samples), averaged over 400 calls: predict_intent 1.0ms, of which the classifier (predict_intent_with_confidence) was 730us and the support scan 134us. The classifier ran two candle Linear ops, a softmax and a copy-out per prompt, about 33K multiply-adds dominated by per-call tensor overhead. Now SusiAlphaModel holds DenseReflex: w1/b1/w2/b2 extracted once at load from the published Linears, with dimensions checked, and probabilities() computes W*x+b -> ReLU -> W*h+b -> softmax (over all outputs, as before) in plain Rust. The defensive rank-0 branch of the old code is gone. Measured after, same setup: classifier 18us, full predict_intent 155us. Test: dense_serving_matches_the_candle_network (max |diff| < 1e-5 against the candle forward for 4 prompts including the empty one). The alpha suite passed 3 of 3 runs and the distill-loop integration test passes. Training still uses candle (ReflexNet).

Iteration 6 — planning can never be served by a reflex (cross-lane ask from Claude). ama::master::plan_steps used GemiEngine::generate_reasoning, which permits Tier-0 reflex serving; a trained reflex whose prompt embedding sits near the wrapped goal (measured cosine 0.72 vs SUPPORT_MIN 0.6) could answer the decomposition request with a bare 'ACTION: status' line, the numbered-step parser drops it, and the mission silently degrades to a single-step plan. Now uses generate_reasoning_deep — planning is deliberation, never a cached answer.
entries.proof: cargo check -p susi-gawd-swarm --all-targets clean; prior suite 59 pass unchanged (one-call-site behavior change).

entries.milestone: Iteration 7 — reflex_served joins served Tier-0/1 actions to mission outcomes (Claude's distill ask). When ReflexEngine serves, reason_internal now records a non-citable 'reflex:<action>' receipt on the active EvidenceSession via capture_call (workspace-bound, works from rayon workers). emit_mission_trace lifts reflex:* tool names into MissionTrace.reflex_served — the trace says which reflex answered, so distill can suppress a served action that repeatedly precedes failures. is_citable_for_mission exempts reflex:* (same class as 'status'): a cached answer must neither certify the mission nor compel citations.
entries.proof: cargo check susi-gemi/susi-core/susi-gawd-swarm clean; mission_trace 9 pass; reflex receipts flow: capture_call -> receipts -> trace.tools + trace.reflex_served.

entries.milestone: Iteration 8 — success_rate(goal, traces) API: Option<f32> fraction of similar missions that succeeded; None for novel intents so callers never misread absence as 0. One number for routing/promotion instead of each consumer recounting similar() results.
entries.proof: success_rate asserted inside retrieval test (1/3 and None arms). mission_trace 9 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 9 — mission_traces.jsonl is now bounded (8 MiB, ~16k records). emit() rotates under the existing FileLock: past the cap the oldest half is dropped starting at a line boundary so readers never see a partial first record. Mirrors Claude's 20k cap on the staging buffer — retrieval reads the whole file per mission, so unbounded growth was a compounding latency cost.
entries.proof: oversized_log_rotates_to_newest_parseable_half: over-cap file shrinks below cap, newest record intact. mission_trace 10 pass.

entries.milestone: Iteration 10 — plan metadata joins the mission trace. SusiMissionReport carries PlanRecord {steps, score, consensus, failed_step}: the abort path records the 1-based failing step; the synthesis-path final report gets the chosen candidate's record attached. MissionTrace gains plan_steps/plan_score/plan_consensus/failed_step (schema v2 defaults keep v1 lines readable) and history_brief annotates similar traces with '[failed at step N]' so planning-time retrieval surfaces where plans broke, not just that they failed.
entries.proof: plan_fields_flow_into_brief_with_step_attribution; susi-core 210 pass, susi-gawd-swarm 59 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 11 — closed the failed-step loop: mission_trace::failed_steps extracts the step text at each similar failure's failed_step index; HistorySignals carries it into deliberate, which docks a candidate -0.15 per step (cap 2) whose token Jaccard with any doomed step is ≥0.6. Plans now steer around the exact step that previously broke, not only away from tainted tools.
entries.proof: steps_echoing_a_doomed_step_are_docked (deliberation); failed_steps_extracts_only_doomed_step_texts (mission_trace). susi-core 211, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 12 — IDF-weighted mission retrieval. `similar` now scores weighted token overlap: document frequency is computed over the trace corpus and each shared token contributes ln((N+1)/(df+1))+1. A shared rare token outranks a shared ubiquitous token; under plain Jaccard 'deploy kubernetes' tied with 'deploy database'. All downstream consumers (brief, difficulty, failing/proven tools, failed steps, success_rate) inherit the better ranking.
entries.proof: idf_ranks_rare_shared_tokens_over_common_ones: rare-token match ranks first while the common-token match drops below the similarity floor. susi-core 212 pass; susi-gawd-swarm 60, susi-gawd green; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 13 — few-shot plan exemplars. proven_plan_brief picks the most similar SUCCESSFUL trace with recorded plan_steps and injects its numbered decomposition into the plan_steps prompt. Failed traces and traces without plan metadata can never become exemplars; novel goals get none. Retrieval now informs the planner of what to copy, not only what to avoid.
entries.proof: proven_plan_brief_only_teaches_from_successes: exemplar carries the winning plan's numbered steps, failed-trace steps excluded, novel goal yields empty brief. susi-core 213, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 14 — unreliable-neighborhood consensus. mission_trace::unreliable_neighborhood (≥2 similar traces, <50% success rate) sets deliberation.consensus_required in solve_autonomous — a mixed track record demands plan agreement even when the intent isn't vetoed and the scope is read-only. success_rate is now consumed by routing decisions, not just exposed.
entries.proof: unreliable_neighborhood_needs_two_neighbors_and_below_half: 0.25 unreliable, 0.5 not, single neighbor too thin, novel intent clean. susi-core 214, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 15 — two cross-lane asks landed. (1) dag.rs node execution now calls generate_reasoning_deep: node templates are dense with capability words and cleared Tier-0's support gate (Claude measured 0.60-0.64), so a served ACTION: line would complete a node having executed nothing. (2) receipt_archive staging_eligible excludes reflex:* receipts — untrainable serves were inflating the staging threshold (Claude's lane file, their proposed fix).
entries.proof: reflex_receipts_never_stage_training_samples: archived but training_staged=None, no staging file. susi-core 219, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 16 — scorer self-measurement. plan_score_correlation computes Pearson r between recorded plan_score and verified outcome across scored traces (>=4 required); solve_autonomous prints score/outcome r in the [RETRIEVAL] line. The scorer is a model like any other — anti-correlated ranking now surfaces as a negative number rather than hiding inside plausible scores.
entries.proof: plan_score_correlation_flags_a_scorer_that_predicts_backwards: r < -0.5 on an inverted scorer; None under 4 scored missions and with no scores. susi-core 220, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 17 — evidence-backed success. MissionTrace::verified() requires succeeded() && evidence_entries > 0. promotion_status, proven_tools, proven_plan_brief and failing_tool_counts treat a receipt-free SUCCESS as neutral: it can no longer promote a reflex, teach tools/plans, condemn tools, or exonerate failing ones.
entries.proof: promotion test asserts unverified SUCCESS → Insufficient{0,0}; teach-path tests updated to verified traces. susi-core 220, susi-gawd 55, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 18 — recency-decayed retrieval. similar() multiplies each trace's IDF similarity by 0.5 + 0.5·e^(-age/τ) with τ = 30 days: a fresh less-similar trace outranks an ancient near-match, while old lessons fade toward half weight rather than dropping to zero. Briefs, difficulty, teach/exonerate paths inherit the ordering.
entries.proof: recency_decay_demotes_stale_near_matches: epoch-1 trace sharing two tokens loses to a fresh one sharing the rare token. susi-core 221, susi-gawd 55, susi-gawd-swarm 60 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 19 — order-aware consensus. plan_similarity compared bag-of-tokens Jaccard, so a plan and its exact reverse scored 1.0 — consensus could approve a mutation executed backwards. Now min(set-similarity, aligned positional step-Jaccard): same work in the same order is required.
entries.proof: plan_similarity_is_order_aware: reversed steps < threshold, identical = 1.0, near-duplicate same-order ≥ threshold. susi-gawd-swarm 61 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 20 — strategy-diverse plan search. style_hint(budget) injects a per-candidate decomposition strategy into plan_steps' prompt: ≤2-step budgets get a minimal-viable-sequence hint, ≥5 get explicit post-mutation verification. Candidates now disagree about approach, not only length — the consensus gate measures approach agreement, not paraphrases of one length choice.
entries.proof: budgets_span_distinct_strategies: hint mapping + max_steps=4 yields three distinct styles. susi-gawd-swarm 62 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 21 — signal-aware history briefs. history_brief annotates [governance-blocked] / [cloud-attempt-failed] on traces carrying GOVERNANCE_BLOCK or CLOUD_ATTEMPT_FAILED signals — refusal classes and failed cloud paths reach the planner instead of sitting unread in trace.signals.
entries.proof: brief_flags_governance_blocked_and_cloud_failed_history: both annotations appear; ordinary signals annotate nothing. susi-core 222 (mission_trace 18) pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 22 — failing_tool_counts counted mentions, not missions: a tool invoked 5× in one failed mission counted 5 failures, inflating the repetition-scaled deliberation penalty up to its cap on a single bad run. Now dedups per mission, matching the documented contract.
entries.proof: flaky_tool listed twice in one FAILED trace counts 1. susi-core 222 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 23 — recency-weighted difficulty. difficulty()'s failure_rate is now weighted by the same 0.5 + 0.5·e^(-age/30d) function used in retrieval ordering (extracted as shared recency_weight). A failure yesterday outweighs one a year old; intents that recovered stop paying full price for ancient failures.
entries.proof: difficulty_weights_recent_failures_heavier: ~0.33 with stale failure + fresh success, ~0.67 flipped. susi-core 223 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 24 — recency-weighted success_rate. The similar-mission success fraction is now weighted by the shared decay, so unreliable_neighborhood sees a stale-success/fresh-failure pair as 0.33 (unreliable) instead of 0.5 (passing).
entries.proof: stale_success_does_not_paper_over_a_fresh_failure: rate ~0.33, neighborhood flagged. susi-core 224 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 25 — duration-aware briefs. duration_secs renders as [~Ns] in history_brief lines, so observed mission cost reaches the planner. Every MissionTrace field is now consumed by a downstream decision or prompt.
entries.proof: brief test asserts [~90s] annotation. susi-core 224 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 26 — failing-agent plan penalty. failing_agent_counts mirrors failing_tool_counts for the agents field: agents appearing only on failed similar missions (never a verified win) merge into HistorySignals.failed in solve_autonomous, so a plan step naming a historically-failing agent is docked like a tainted tool.
entries.proof: failing_agent_counts_track_missions_and_clear_on_verified_wins: dedup per mission, exonerated by verified success. susi-core 225, susi-gawd-swarm 62 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 27 — proven-step bonus, mirror of the doomed-step penalty. mission_trace::proven_steps collects step texts from verified-successful similar missions; HistorySignals.proven_steps lets deliberate award +0.05 per candidate step echoing one (cap 3). Plans now lean toward moves that demonstrably worked, not only away from moves that broke.
entries.proof: steps_echoing_a_proven_step_earn_a_bonus. susi-core 225, susi-gawd-swarm 63 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 28 — proven-agent bonus. proven_agents collects agents appearing only on verified-successful similar missions (ambiguous/unverified excluded); they merge into HistorySignals.proven in solve_autonomous so plan steps naming a trusted agent earn the proven bonus. Completes the agent-level history signal.
entries.proof: proven_agents_excludes_ambiguous_and_unverified: verified-only wins proven; failed-agent and bare-claim excluded. susi-core 226, susi-gawd-swarm 63 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 29 — PlanRecord attribution. Iter-10 recorded candidates[0].score and the initial plan's steps unconditionally: after a read-scope replan (candidate 2 succeeding) or the unapproved single-step fallback, the trace joined the wrong plan to the outcome. Now tracks the executed candidate across the attempts loop and looks its score up (or scores the fallback directly).

Iteration 30 — intra-plan duplicate penalty. Plan scoring docks -0.05 per step that is a near-duplicate (token Jaccard ≥ 0.8) of an earlier step: repeated steps waste execution, and a plan that repeats itself should lose to a varied one.
entries.proof: near_duplicate_steps_are_penalized: literal repeat scores lower and reports duplicate_steps=1. susi-gawd-swarm 64 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 31 — paraphrase-proof promotion. promotion_status matched token signatures exactly, so 'deploy the api backend' escaped the veto after 'deploy the api' failed. Matching now includes token-Jaccard ≥ 0.6 paraphrases: near-identical phrasings share the habit's record for both veto and success counting.
entries.proof: promotion test: paraphrase of recently-failed intent → Vetoed; unrelated intent unaffected. susi-core 227 pass; clippy clean.

entries.milestone: Iteration 32 — risk-scaled consensus. All gated intents demanded the same 0.35 top-two agreement; now the bar scales: High/Critical risk 0.55, Mutate/SelfExtend scope 0.45, read-only 0.35. The applied threshold is stored on Deliberation and logged, so gate decisions stay auditable.
entries.proof: consensus_threshold_scales_with_risk: a 0.5-similarity pair is rejected for a High-risk intent yet approved for a Medium mutating one. susi-gawd-swarm 65 pass; clippy clean.
